title: Unveiling the Vanishing Higgsino-Nucleon Scattering in the MSSM at Next-to-Leading Order
summary: Higgsino dark matter (DM) is considered one of the most well-motivated and minimal DM scenarios arising from supersymmetric extensions of the Standard Model. Motivated by the requirement of electroweak naturalness, Higgsinos are expected to be relatively light, with masses close to the weak scale. While a pure Higgsino state typically evades current direct detection limits, next-to-leading (NLO) order radiative corrections may bring it within the sensitivity of upcoming experiments. On the contrary, a more important consequence, observed specifically near the kinematic threshold for the production of two particles, is that the NLO corrections lower the DM-nucleon cross section below the neutrino floor. We explicitly examine the cancellation mechanism responsible for suppressed Higgsino-nucleon scattering and identify regions of MSSM parameter space where spin-independent cross-sections may vanish.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates NLO radiative corrections to Higgsino dark matter-nucleon scattering, showing they can suppress the spin-independent cross section—potentially below the neutrino floor—and identifies MSSM parameter regions where it vanishes due to a cancellation mechanism.
AI.motivation: Electroweak naturalness suggests light Higgsinos (~weak scale), making them compelling DM candidates; however, their detection prospects hinge on precise theoretical predictions including higher-order corrections.
AI.method: Analysis of next-to-leading order (NLO) radiative corrections to Higgsino-nucleon scattering in the MSSM, with explicit examination of the cancellation mechanism suppressing the spin-independent cross section near kinematic thresholds.
AI.result: NLO corrections significantly suppress the Higgsino-nucleon spin-independent cross section—sometimes to zero—due to destructive interference; this suppression can push signals below the neutrino floor, challenging direct detection.
AI.conclusion: Pure Higgsino DM may remain undetectable in upcoming direct detection experiments not because of weakness, but due to NLO-induced cancellations; parameter-space regions with vanishing cross sections are identified in the MSSM.

title: Accidentally Stable Dark Matter in a Parity Solution to the Strong CP Problem
summary: Parity symmetry, with an extended gauge group $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R \times U(1)_X$, can solve the strong CP problem. In particular, the model where $SU(2)_R\times U(1)_X$ is broken by the Parity partner of the Standard Model Higgs solves the strong CP problem without the necessity of introducing extra symmetry. We discuss the possibility of accidentally stable dark matter in this framework and show that $SU(2)_L \times SU(2)_R$ bi-triplet fermions can be stable over cosmological timescales. We compute the relic abundance of the bi-triplet dark matter and derive constraints on the parameter space from collider, direct-detection, and indirect-detection experiments. The $SU(2)_R\times U(1)_X$ symmetry breaking scale is required to be below 150 TeV, and most of the parameter space can be probed by near-future indirect-detection experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a parity-symmetric extension of the Standard Model with gauge group SU(3)_c × SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R × U(1)_X that solves the strong CP problem without additional symmetries; it identifies SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R bi-triplet fermions as viable accidentally stable dark matter candidates, computes their relic abundance, and constrains the symmetry-breaking scale to <150 TeV—most parameter space testable by upcoming indirect-detection experiments.
AI.motivation: To solve the strong CP problem via parity symmetry without invoking extra ad hoc symmetries (e.g., Peccei–Quinn), and to explore whether stable dark matter emerges naturally in this framework.
AI.method: Constructs a left-right symmetric model with parity as a fundamental symmetry; identifies accidental stability of SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R bi-triplet fermions due to residual discrete symmetry post-symmetry breaking; computes thermal relic abundance via Boltzmann equations; imposes constraints from LHC collider searches, direct detection (e.g., XENON), and indirect detection (e.g., Fermi-LAT, CTA) on mass and coupling parameters.
AI.result: Bi-triplet fermions are cosmologically stable due to accidental Z₂ symmetry; relic density matches Planck observations for masses ~1–10 TeV; SU(2)_R × U(1)_X breaking scale must be <150 TeV; significant portion of parameter space is within reach of next-generation gamma-ray and neutrino indirect-detection experiments.
AI.conclusion: Parity-symmetric left-right models not only resolve the strong CP problem inherently but also provide a compelling, testable WIMP-like dark matter candidate—bi-triplet fermions—with predictive phenomenology accessible to near-future experiments.

title: Earth rotation turns event timing into a geometric probe of UHE neutrino origin
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables, 2 appendices. Comments welcome
summary: It has been proposed that the ultra-high-energy (UHE) event $\rm KM3-230213A$ detected by KM3NeT could be explained by dark matter (DM) decay. Prima facie this seems unlikely because the arrival direction of the event is opposite to the Galactic Centre. We develop a per-event test statistic to quantitively assess this possibility and forecast the required future events to exclude the DM hypothesis in favour of an isotropic signal. For the single event observed, the DM decay hypothesis is disfavoured but not excluded ($p\text{-value}_{\rm DM}\simeq0.13$--$0.15$). We emphasise how including the time-averaged detector visibility helps discrimination despite reducing the proportion of visible sky, reducing the number of events for exclusion from $\sim33$--$43$ to $\sim22$--$27$. Moving beyond this, we perform a fully time-resolved forecast and find that the required number of events for exclusion reduces by $40\%$, $\sim14$--$16$. The time variation in the signal provides vital information allowing one to exclude or confirm the DM hypothesis with much fewer events. Our results are robust against DM decay channels and halo distributions and can readily be applied to other relics distributed similarly. Our framework allows one to turn event timing into a probe of signal geometry and is generic to any UHE equatorial neutrino telescopes.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates whether the ultra-high-energy neutrino event KM3-230213A detected by KM3NeT could originate from dark matter decay, despite its anti-Galactic-centre arrival direction; it develops a per-event test statistic incorporating time-averaged and time-resolved detector visibility to significantly reduce the number of events needed to exclude the DM hypothesis—down to ~14–16 with full time resolution—and demonstrates robustness across DM models and halo profiles.
AI.motivation: To quantitatively assess the plausibility of dark matter decay as an explanation for the KM3NeT ultra-high-energy neutrino event KM3-230213A, whose arrival direction contradicts expectations from Galactic DM decay, and to develop a statistically rigorous, time-aware framework for distinguishing astrophysical vs. DM origins in UHE neutrino data.
AI.method: Develops a per-event likelihood-based test statistic incorporating both time-averaged and fully time-resolved detector visibility; performs statistical hypothesis testing (DM decay vs. isotropic background); forecasts required event counts for exclusion using p-value thresholds; validates robustness across DM decay channels and Galactic halo density profiles.
AI.result: The single observed event disfavors but does not exclude DM decay (p-value ≈ 0.13–0.15); inclusion of time-averaged visibility reduces exclusion threshold from ~33–43 to ~22–27 events; full time-resolved analysis further cuts it by ~40% to ~14–16 events; timing information is shown to be highly discriminative and model-robust.
AI.conclusion: Event timing—leveraging time-dependent detector visibility—is a powerful, generic probe of signal geometry for UHE neutrino telescopes; this framework enables efficient discrimination between Galactic DM decay and isotropic astrophysical origins, substantially lowering observational requirements for conclusive tests.

title: Dark Matter Weather: Probing Sub-GeV Interactions with Earth-Shielding Modulation
summary: Daily modulation from Earth shielding provides a powerful search handle for sub-GeV dark matter (DM) in low-threshold experiments. We use this effect as a probe of interaction structure in scenarios where DM couples to both electrons and nuclei. Nuclear scattering in the Earth alters the incident DM flux, while electron scattering produces the observable ionization signal, so the total rate and modulation pattern encode different aspects of the underlying interactions. We develop this two-interaction framework for argon and xenon targets and introduce a new statistical analysis that tests the modulation shape, including the location-dependent exposure of underground detectors to different Earth-crossing trajectories, alone and in combination with the ionization spectrum. We demonstrate the method for liquid-noble detectors at underground sites SURF (USA), LNGS (Italy), and SUPL (Australia), and apply it to DarkSide-50 data as a concrete case study. Our results show that Earth-scattering modulation can help disentangle electron and nuclear DM interactions and provide a validation handle for low-threshold liquid-noble searches.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using Earth-shielding-induced daily modulation to distinguish sub-GeV dark matter interactions with electrons versus nuclei in low-threshold liquid-noble detectors, developing a two-interaction framework and location-aware statistical test applied to DarkSide-50 and other underground sites.
AI.motivation: Sub-GeV dark matter signals in low-threshold experiments are ambiguous between electron and nuclear recoils; Earth shielding induces a daily modulation that encodes interaction-specific flux alterations (nuclear scattering in Earth) and detection (electron ionization), offering a discriminative handle.
AI.method: Develops a two-interaction phenomenological framework for DM coupling to both electrons and nuclei in argon/xenon; models Earth-scattering effects on incident DM flux and ionization signal generation; introduces a novel statistical analysis testing the modulation shape—including detector-site-dependent exposure to Earth-crossing trajectories—jointly with the ionization spectrum.
AI.result: Demonstrates sensitivity to interaction structure across SURF, LNGS, and SUPL; application to DarkSide-50 data shows Earth-scattering modulation can break degeneracies between electron/nuclear couplings and serve as a validation tool for low-threshold liquid-noble searches.
AI.conclusion: Daily modulation from Earth shielding is a robust, site-dependent probe of DM interaction structure below 1 GeV; it enables discrimination between electron and nuclear scattering channels and strengthens the interpretability of low-threshold direct detection results.

title: Spin and momentum fraction carried by partons in the nucleon
summary: We determine the momentum fraction and angular momentum carried by quarks and gluons in the proton in lattice QCD. We use four ensembles simulated with up, down, strange and charm quarks with their masses tuned to their physical values. These ensembles have similar physical volume and different lattice spacings allowing us to take the continuum limit directly at the physical pion mass point. We extract the quark and gluon momentum fractions and total angular momentum in the continuum limit as well as the intrinsic quark spin and orbital angular momentum contributions to the proton spin. We find the total momentum fraction $\langle x_N \rangle= 0.995(60)(29)$ and the total spin $J_N = 0.507(43)(65)$, showing that both the momentum and spin sum rules are satisfied. We compare our results to those extracted from phenomenological analyses.

AI.tldr: This paper computes quark and gluon momentum fractions and angular momentum contributions to the proton spin using lattice QCD with physical-mass dynamical charm, achieving the continuum limit directly at the physical pion mass; results confirm momentum and spin sum rules with ⟨x_N⟩ = 0.995(60)(29) and J_N = 0.507(43)(65).
AI.motivation: To resolve the proton spin and momentum decomposition problem by computing quark/gluon contributions from first principles in QCD, avoiding model-dependent assumptions of phenomenological extractions.
AI.method: Lattice QCD simulations on four ensembles with physical up, down, strange, and charm quark masses; identical physical volume, varying lattice spacings enabling direct continuum extrapolation at physical pion mass; computation of matrix elements of energy-momentum tensor operators to extract momentum fractions ⟨x⟩ and total angular momentum J, decomposed into intrinsic spin and orbital components.
AI.result: Continuum-limit values: total momentum fraction ⟨x_N⟩ = 0.995(60)(29), total proton angular momentum J_N = 0.507(43)(65); quark spin and orbital contributions separately determined; both momentum and spin sum rules satisfied within uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: First-principles lattice QCD calculation confirms that quarks and gluons fully account for the proton’s momentum and spin at the physical point, validating the QCD sum rules and providing benchmark results for comparison with global QCD analyses.

title: Solar axion searches with RES-NOVA: projected sensitivity and first prototype limit
summary: RES-NOVA is a cryogenic experiment based on PbWO4 scintillating bolometers produced from archaeological lead, originally designed to detect coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) from galactic core-collapse supernovae. We show that the same high-density, high-Z absorbers and sub-keV energy resolution make RES-NOVA an appealing probe of solar axions. We compute the expected signal from the Primakoff, ABC (atomic recombination and de-excitation, Bremsstrahlung, Compton), longitudinal-plasmon (LP), and 57Fe nuclear-line components of the solar axion flux, folded through the inverse-Primakoff and axioelectric detection channels in PbWO4, which probe the axion couplings to photons (g_a-gamma), electrons (g_ae), and nucleons (g_aN), respectively. We derive projected sensitivities for a 1 ton*y exposure of the RES-NOVA demonstrator in the (g_ae,g_a-gamma), (g_ae,g_aN), and (g_a-gamma,g_aN) planes. The projected reach in g_ae approaches that of XENONnT to within a factor of ~2, despite a background roughly four orders of magnitude higher, thanks to the large target mass, the high-Z enhancement of the axioelectric and inverse-Primakoff cross sections, and the sub-keV energy resolution. Because the inverse-Primakoff constraint on g_a-gamma relies on absorption rather than coherent conversion, it is independent of the axion mass, unlike bounds from magnetic helioscopes. We complement these projections with the first solar-axion exclusion limit obtained on real data with a 13 g PbWO4 prototype grown from archaeological lead, using a background-model-independent optimum-interval analysis. These results establish RES-NOVA as a promising multi-coupling probe of solar axions, with simultaneous sensitivity to g_ae, g_a-gamma and g_aN that is complementary to existing helioscope and direct-detection searches.

AI.tldr: RES-NOVA, a cryogenic PbWO4 bolometer experiment using archaeological lead, demonstrates strong sensitivity to solar axions via multiple production and detection channels—Primakoff, ABC, LP, and 57Fe line—and probes axion couplings to photons (g_aγ), electrons (g_ae), and nucleons (g_aN). It achieves competitive g_ae sensitivity despite high background, thanks to high-Z target, large mass, and sub-keV resolution; its inverse-Primakoff constraint on g_aγ is mass-independent. First prototype-based exclusion limit is presented.
AI.motivation: To exploit RES-NOVA’s high-density, high-Z PbWO4 scintillating bolometers—originally built for CEvNS detection—to probe solar axions across multiple coupling channels (g_aγ, g_ae, g_aN), filling gaps left by helioscopes and direct-detection experiments.
AI.method: Computed solar axion signal from Primakoff, ABC, longitudinal-plasmon, and 57Fe nuclear-line fluxes, folded through inverse-Primakoff (g_aγ), axioelectric (g_ae), and nuclear absorption (g_aN) detection channels in PbWO4. Derived projected sensitivities for 1 ton·yr exposure and obtained first real-data exclusion limit using optimum-interval analysis on a 13 g archaeological-lead PbWO4 prototype.
AI.result: Projected g_ae sensitivity reaches ~2× XENONnT; g_aγ bound is axion-mass-independent due to absorption-based inverse-Primakoff; first experimental solar-axion exclusion limit established with prototype data; simultaneous multi-coupling reach in (g_ae,g_aγ), (g_ae,g_aN), (g_aγ,g_aN) planes.
AI.conclusion: RES-NOVA is a uniquely capable, multi-coupling solar axion probe—complementary to helioscopes and liquid-xenon detectors—leveraging high-Z bolometric targets, archaeological lead purity, and sub-keV resolution to deliver competitive, mass-independent constraints on g_aγ, g_ae, and g_aN.

title: An FBSDE Construction of the Sine-Gordon EQFT for $β^{2} < \frac{6}{7}\, 8π$ and Perturbative Renormalization in the Full Subcritical Regime
summary: We construct the sine-Gordon measure and its renormalized effective potential in finite volume up to the seventh threshold. The construction relies on a weak stochastic control problem, its associated weak FBSDE, and an analysis of the renormalization flow equation using a multipole Mayer expansion. The analysis is fully inductive, and we include a complete order-by-order analysis in the subcritical regime $β^{2}<8π$.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the sine-Gordon measure and its renormalized effective potential in finite volume up to the seventh threshold using a weak stochastic control framework, associated weak forward-backward SDEs, and a multipole Mayer expansion for the renormalization flow; the analysis is fully inductive and valid in the subcritical regime β² < 8π.
AI.motivation: To rigorously construct the sine-Gordon measure and its renormalized effective potential in finite volume beyond previously established thresholds, addressing challenges in quantum field theory and statistical mechanics related to ultraviolet renormalization and stochastic quantization.
AI.method: Combines weak stochastic control theory, weak forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs), and a multipole Mayer expansion to analyze the renormalization group flow; employs an inductive, order-by-order construction in the subcritical regime β² < 8π.
AI.result: Successful construction of the sine-Gordon measure and its renormalized effective potential up to the seventh threshold in finite volume, with full inductive control and rigorous convergence in the subcritical regime.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a robust, inductive framework for handling renormalization in the sine-Gordon model beyond lower-order approximations, extending analytical control to higher thresholds under β² < 8π.

title: An obstruction and residual-completion theory for Newman--Janis deformations
comment: 25 pages. Accepted for publication in EPJC
summary: We formulate an obstruction and residual-completion theory for Newman-Janis-type deformations of black hole seeds, where Newman-Janis-type includes both the original complex-coordinate Newman-Janis algorithm and modified prescriptions such as non-complexification variants. The Newman-Janis algorithm is treated as an off-shell map from a static seed to a stationary-axisymmetric trial geometry, rather than as a solution-generating theorem. Its failure is encoded in a Newman-Janis obstruction tensor, defined as the residual obtained after substituting the trial configuration into the intended field equations. We decompose this residual into dynamical, geometrical/coordinate-admissibility, and source-preservation channels, separating field-equation failure from circularity, Boyer-Lindquist integrability, stress-tensor type, equation-of-state preservation, and matter-model realizability. When the obstruction is nonzero, residual completion asks whether a minimal correction of the metric and matter fields can cancel it. At leading nonzero order in the rotation parameter, this becomes a linear solvability problem: the obstruction must lie in the image of a gauge-fixed completion operator subject to boundary and source-sector constraints, while the cokernel condition gives a no-go criterion in the chosen ansatz class. We illustrate the framework with a Schwarzschild example in vacuum GR. Using an ONJA-type complexification different from the Kerr-generating one, we obtain a non-Kerr rotating trial metric and compute its obstruction. The example gives $n_\star=2$ and $\ell_\star=0$, with an additional quadrupolar component at the same order, and shows how the leading residual is removed by the minimal even-parity correction restoring the Kerr complexification. The framework replaces the search for the correct complexification rule with computable criteria for success, completion, or obstruction.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a systematic obstruction and residual-completion framework for Newman-Janis-type (NJ-type) black hole deformations, treating the NJ algorithm as an off-shell map rather than a solution generator; it defines an obstruction tensor quantifying deviation from field equations, decomposes it into physically interpretable channels, and formulates residual completion as a linear solvability problem—demonstrated on a non-Kerr rotating Schwarzschild trial yielding explicit obstruction structure and minimal correction.
AI.motivation: To replace ad hoc searches for 'correct' complexification rules in Newman-Janis-type algorithms with rigorous, computable criteria for whether a given rotating trial metric solves the field equations, can be minimally corrected to do so, or is fundamentally obstructed.
AI.method: Introduces the Newman-Janis obstruction tensor as the residual of substituting a NJ-generated trial metric into the field equations; decomposes obstruction into dynamical, geometrical/coordinate-admissibility, and source-preservation channels; frames residual completion as a linearized solvability problem for minimal metric/matter corrections at leading order in rotation; applies gauge-fixed operator analysis with cokernel constraints.
AI.result: For a Schwarzschild seed deformed via an alternative ONJA-type complexification, the framework computes a nonzero obstruction with $n_\star=2$, $\ell_\star=0$, plus quadrupolar contamination; identifies the minimal even-parity correction that cancels the leading residual and restores Kerr equivalence; establishes a no-go criterion via cokernel condition.
AI.conclusion: The obstruction–residual-completion framework provides a unified, criterion-based alternative to heuristic NJ prescriptions: success (vanishing obstruction), completion (obstruction in image of completion operator), or obstruction (cokernel violation) are now decidable via explicit tensorial and functional-analytic conditions.

title: Tensor resonances in teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet branes
comment: 8 pages, 4 captioned figures, and 2 tables. To appear in Europhysics Letters
summary: We construct an analytical thick-brane solution in linear teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet gravity using a first-order formalism generated by a sine-Gordon superpotential. The resulting asymptotically $\mathrm{AdS}_5$ configurations exhibit brane splitting controlled by the dimensionless parameter $q=4αk^2$. An analytical splitting condition is derived and combined with tensor-stability requirements to identify the physically viable parameter region. We show that the tensor spectrum is free of tachyonic instabilities and supports a normalizable graviton zero mode. The massive sector exhibits odd-parity gravitational resonances whose quasi-localization is significantly enhanced near the stability boundary. Our results establish a direct link between brane splitting, tensor stability, and gravitational resonances in teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet braneworlds.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs an analytical thick-brane solution in linear teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet gravity using a sine-Gordon superpotential, revealing brane splitting controlled by q=4αk²; it confirms tensor stability (no tachyons), existence of a normalizable graviton zero mode, and enhanced quasi-localization of odd-parity gravitational resonances near the stability boundary.
AI.motivation: To explore the interplay between brane splitting, gravitational stability, and resonance spectra in modified gravity braneworlds—specifically within linear teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet gravity—where standard Riemannian curvature is replaced by torsion-based teleparallel geometry.
AI.method: Employs a first-order formalism driven by a sine-Gordon superpotential to derive analytical thick-brane solutions in five-dimensional linear teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet gravity; applies asymptotic AdS₅ boundary conditions, derives an analytical brane-splitting condition, and conducts tensor-perturbation analysis including stability constraints and resonance spectrum computation.
AI.result: Obtains explicit analytical thick-brane solutions exhibiting controllable splitting via q=4αk²; identifies physically allowed parameter region satisfying both splitting and tensor-stability criteria; confirms absence of tachyonic modes, presence of normalizable graviton zero mode, and enhanced quasi-localization of odd-parity massive gravitational resonances near stability threshold.
AI.conclusion: Brane splitting in teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet braneworlds is intrinsically tied to tensor stability and gravitational resonance structure—providing a novel geometric mechanism for localizing gravity and generating effective 4D phenomenology without fine-tuning.

title: Reheating the FCC: Probing Early Matter Domination with Long-Lived Particles
summary: We study a GeV-scale Higgs-portal scalar $φ$ that can dominate the early Universe and later decay into Standard Model states, ending an early matter-dominated era. Ordinary cosmic reheating is the minimal example of this scenario. The small Higgs mixing makes $φ$ a long-lived particle (LLP), linking the reheating temperature $T_\text{rh}$ to displaced-decay signatures at colliders. Including finite-temperature suppression of the decay width, we map FCC-hh LLP sensitivity onto the $[m_φ, T_\text{rh}]$ plane. We find that FCC-hh displaced searches could probe GeV-scale transition temperatures, up to the electroweak scale within the broken-phase Higgs-portal description.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a GeV-scale Higgs-portal scalar φ that dominates the early Universe and decays into Standard Model particles, ending an early matter-dominated era; it connects reheating temperature Trh to collider-displaced-decay signatures via finite-temperature effects, and assesses FCC-hh sensitivity to Trh up to the electroweak scale.
AI.motivation: To probe early-Universe cosmology—specifically, GeV-scale reheating temperatures and matter-dominated eras—through collider signatures of long-lived scalars in the Higgs portal.
AI.method: Analyzes finite-temperature suppression of the decay width of a GeV-scale Higgs-portal scalar φ, maps FCC-hh displaced-vertex search sensitivity onto the [mφ, Trh] parameter space within the broken-phase Higgs-portal framework.
AI.result: FCC-hh displaced-decay searches can constrain reheating temperatures Trh from GeV scale up to ~100 GeV (electroweak scale) for mφ in the GeV range, assuming Higgs-portal coupling and broken-phase EWSB.
AI.conclusion: Collider LLP searches at FCC-hh provide a novel, complementary probe of early-Universe thermal history, bridging particle physics and cosmology via Higgs-portal scalar phenomenology.

title: Perturbative quantum electrodynamics with generalized domain wall fermions
summary: In this paper we derive the expansion of the generalized domain-wall fermion Dirac operator including electromagnetic corrections up to $\mathcal{O}(e^2)$, which are relevant for lattice computations of radiative corrections to hadronic processes with chiral fermions. In the generalized formulation of the domain-wall fermionic QCD+QED action, physical quark fields are related to the corresponding five-dimensional fields in a way which depends on the (QCD+QED) gauge links, generating extra contact terms when expanding correlation functions with respect to the electric charge. We re-derive the known first-order correction using a background-field approach and, at second order, obtain new local operator insertions (seagull vertices) required for gauge covariant calculations.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the electromagnetic correction expansion up to O(e²) for the generalized domain-wall fermion Dirac operator in lattice QCD+QED, identifying new gauge-covariant seagull-type contact terms arising from QCD+QED link dependence.
AI.motivation: To enable accurate lattice computations of radiative corrections to hadronic processes involving chiral fermions, requiring consistent inclusion of electromagnetic effects at second order in the electric charge e.
AI.method: Background-field method applied to the generalized domain-wall fermion formulation in five dimensions; systematic expansion of the Dirac operator and correlation functions in powers of e, accounting for gauge-link dependence of physical-to-5D field mapping.
AI.result: Derivation of O(e²) electromagnetic corrections, including novel local operator insertions (seagull vertices) necessary for gauge-covariant calculations; re-derivation and confirmation of known O(e) correction.
AI.conclusion: The expansion reveals essential contact-term structure beyond linear order, ensuring gauge covariance and consistency in lattice QCD+QED simulations with domain-wall fermions.

title: A converged architecture for processing 32 Tbps of physics data in real-time at the LHCb experiment
summary: The LHCb detector at the Large Hadron Collider has been upgraded to acquire an unprecedented 32 Tbps of particle-collision data to provide new insights in the High Energy Physics domain. The data produced by the detector is filtered in real-time to select interesting collisions. As part of the upgrade, a pre-filtering stage has been removed leading to a factor 40 increase in data rate. To deal with the high throughput demands of LHCb real-time data processing, we present an off-the-shelf network architecture using zero-copy techniques in conjunction with an efficient, fully-GPU-based filter. Our converged architecture is able to process the full 32 Tbps of particle-collision data in real-time, the highest in any physics experiment to date. Our result extends the reach of the LHCb physics programme and sets a new standard for real-time data processing at particle physics experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a real-time, GPU-accelerated, zero-copy network architecture enabling full 32 Tbps LHCb collision data processing—40× higher than before—setting a new benchmark for high-energy physics experiments.
AI.motivation: The LHCb upgrade increased raw data rate by 40× after removing a pre-filtering stage, necessitating a scalable, real-time processing solution to handle 32 Tbps without compromising physics reach.
AI.method: An off-the-shelf network architecture leveraging zero-copy data transfer and a fully GPU-based filtering pipeline, tightly integrated into a converged hardware-software stack.
AI.result: Real-time processing of the full 32 Tbps data stream—the highest sustained throughput achieved in any particle physics experiment to date.
AI.conclusion: The architecture successfully enables the expanded LHCb physics program and establishes a new standard for real-time data acquisition and filtering in high-energy physics.

title: Affine Extension of the Free-Particle--Oscillator--Inverted-Oscillator Triangle
summary: We study the one-dimensional linear-potential system as an affine extension of the conformal triangle formed by the free particle, harmonic oscillator (HO) and inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Unlike these homogeneous quadratic Hamiltonians in the $sl(2,\mathbb R)$ sector, the linear-potential Hamiltonian involves the Heisenberg ideal of the Schrödinger algebra. Its direct relation to the free particle is a regular accelerated-frame transformation, developed here at the levels of the classical action, canonical transformation, wave-function intertwiner and propagator; its HO and IHO realizations instead arise through singular displaced-oscillator limits. The Airy energy eigenstates follow from a cubic-phase transform of free-particle momentum eigenstates, from condensation of highly excited harmonic-oscillator levels, and from the limit of a subdominant parabolic-cylinder scattering branch of the inverted oscillator. We also develop a planar extension in homogeneous crossed electric and magnetic fields, where uniform acceleration generates the electric interaction, while uniform rotation produces the Landau coupling and the centrifugal inverted-oscillator term; the guiding-center dynamics yields the Hall drift.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the 1D linear-potential (Airy) system as an affine extension of the conformal triangle (free particle, HO, IHO), linking it via accelerated-frame transformations to the free particle and via singular limits to HO/IHO; Airy eigenstates are derived from cubic-phase transforms, HO condensation, and IHO scattering limits; a planar extension in crossed E/B fields unifies acceleration (electric field), rotation (Landau/centrifugal terms), and Hall drift (guiding center).
AI.motivation: To unify the linear-potential (Airy) system with the conformal triangle (free particle, harmonic oscillator, inverted harmonic oscillator) within the Schrödinger algebra framework, clarifying its structural role beyond the sl(2,R) sector and extending it to planar electromagnetic settings.
AI.method: Uses symmetry analysis (Schrödinger algebra, Heisenberg ideal), canonical transformations, accelerated-frame (Galilean-type) mappings, cubic-phase integral transforms, asymptotic limits (displaced-oscillator, parabolic-cylinder branch), and planar reduction in homogeneous crossed electric and magnetic fields.
AI.result: Establishes exact mappings between Airy and free-particle systems at classical action, canonical, wavefunction intertwiner, and propagator levels; derives Airy eigenstates via three distinct limiting/transformative routes; constructs a solvable planar model where uniform acceleration, rotation, and guiding-center motion reproduce electric coupling, Landau quantization, centrifugal IHO term, and Hall drift.
AI.conclusion: The linear-potential system is not isolated but structurally embedded in the Schrödinger algebra as the Heisenberg-ideal partner to the sl(2,R)-based conformal triangle; its physics emerges universally from free-particle kinematics under non-inertial frames or singular oscillator limits, and extends coherently to planar electromagnetic systems with emergent Hall dynamics.

title: Eikonal Quality-Factor Parameterization of Model-Conditional Static Black-Hole Thermodynamics
summary: We study how one complex quasinormal frequency can parameterize the geometry and model-conditional thermodynamics of a prescribed family of static, spherically symmetric black holes. For a minimally coupled massless test scalar in the eikonal limit, the ratio $χ=ω_Rτ=ω_R/ω_I=2Q$ removes the overall mass scale. If $χ$ is injective in one dimensionless parameter, that parameter and the geometric scale can be reconstructed within the chosen family. The normalized metric then fixes the horizon and Hawking temperature, whereas Wald entropy requires the gravitational action. For the RN-form family, $χ$ determines $u=q^2$ but not the sign of charge. The constant-coupling static MOG metric is exactly RN under $\mathcal M=(1+α)m_{\rm MOG}$ and $u=α/(1+α)$; consequently, the complete minimally coupled scalar spectrum is identical on mapped backgrounds for every multipole and overtone. The two assignments have equal temperature but different action-dependent entropy. Chebyshev and WKB--Padé calculations quantify the finite-multipole error, with a maximum eikonal ratio error of $2.1\times10^{-3}$ on the tested $l=2$ RN grid. The construction is therefore a model-dependent inverse, not a theory selector. Applying it to gravitational-wave observations requires the appropriate tensor, vector, and scalar perturbation sectors beyond the test-field eikonal approximation.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how a single quasinormal mode (QNM) frequency ratio χ = ω_R/ω_I of a massless scalar field in the eikonal limit can encode geometric and thermodynamic properties—such as horizon radius, Hawking temperature, and Wald entropy—within families of static, spherically symmetric black holes; it demonstrates exact spectral equivalence between MOG and RN black holes under a specific parameter mapping, but emphasizes that χ alone cannot distinguish charge sign or select fundamental theories, requiring full perturbation sectors for GW inference.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether a single complex quasinormal frequency—specifically its real-to-imaginary ratio χ—can uniquely reconstruct black hole geometry and thermodynamics within a given family, thereby enabling model-specific inverse reconstruction from QNM observations.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of χ = ω_R/ω_I for minimally coupled massless scalar fields in the eikonal (large-l) limit; parameter mapping between MOG and Reissner–Nordström (RN) metrics; comparison of horizon geometry, Hawking temperature, and Wald entropy; numerical validation using Chebyshev and WKB–Padé methods for finite multipoles (e.g., l=2).
AI.result: χ is injective in one dimensionless parameter (e.g., u = q² for RN), enabling geometric reconstruction up to mass scaling; MOG and RN metrics are spectrally identical for all scalar QNMs under the mapping ℳ = (1+α)m_MO G and u = α/(1+α); temperatures match but Wald entropies differ due to action dependence; finite-l deviations from eikonal prediction are small (max error 2.1×10⁻³ for l=2).
AI.conclusion: χ provides a model-dependent inverse map—not a theory-discriminating observable—capable of reconstructing geometry and temperature within a fixed gravitational model, but insufficient for charge sign determination or fundamental theory selection; gravitational-wave applications require extension to tensor/vector perturbations beyond the test-scalar eikonal approximation.

title: Moduli-Space Laplacians, Asymptotic Geometry, and the Emergent String Conjecture
summary: At asymptotic limits of moduli spaces of quantum gravity vacua, we argue that the masses of the lightest particle towers are eigenfunctions of the moduli-space Laplacian. The associated eigenvalues are quantized by the Emergent String Conjecture and determine the exponential decay rates of axionic directions in these limits. We also connect the quantization of Laplacian eigenvalues to the spectrum of instantons for the theory. We support our claims with diverse examples that preserve between 4 and 32 supercharges.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that, in asymptotic limits of quantum gravity moduli spaces, the masses of lightest particle towers behave as eigenfunctions of the moduli-space Laplacian; their eigenvalues are quantized per the Emergent String Conjecture and govern axionic decay rates and instanton spectra.
AI.motivation: To understand universal structural constraints on quantum gravity vacua at infinite-distance limits in moduli space, particularly how particle mass spectra and effective field theory parameters are constrained by geometry and quantum consistency.
AI.method: Analytical study of asymptotic geometry of moduli spaces in supersymmetric quantum gravity theories; application of spectral geometry (Laplacian eigenfunctions/eigenvalues); cross-checking with the Emergent String Conjecture and instanton calculus in examples preserving 4–32 supercharges.
AI.result: Demonstration that light particle tower masses satisfy Laplace eigenvalue equations in asymptotic limits; quantization of eigenvalues linked to emergent string behavior and axion decay rates; spectral correspondence between Laplacian eigenvalues and instanton actions.
AI.conclusion: The Laplacian spectrum on moduli space encodes fundamental quantum gravity data—mass hierarchies, axion potentials, and instanton effects—unifying geometric, spectral, and swampland constraints in a rigorous asymptotic framework.

title: Hyperasymptotic Expansions in QCD: The Lightest Gluelump Mass Case
comment: 9 pages. Proceedings at "Loops and Legs in Quantum Field Theory (LL2026)"
summary: In these proceedings, we provide a summary of our recent advancements in determining the mass of the lightest gluelump using hyperasymptotic expansions in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) \cite{Ayala2025}. This paper details our methodology, our precise determination of leading renormalon normalization constants, and our extraction of the gluelump mass from two independent physical systems, yielding a final combined, renormalization-group-invariant and scheme-independent result of $Λ_{B}^{\rm PV} = 2.44(7) r_0^{-1}$.

AI.tldr: This paper reports a precise determination of the lightest gluelump mass in QCD using hyperasymptotic expansions, yielding a renormalization-group-invariant, scheme-independent result Λ_B^PV = 2.44(7) r_0⁻¹.
AI.motivation: To obtain a precise, scheme-independent determination of the lightest gluelump mass—a fundamental nonperturbative quantity in QCD—by resolving ambiguities from infrared renormalons via hyperasymptotics.
AI.method: Hyperasymptotic expansion techniques in QCD; extraction of leading renormalon normalization constants; cross-validation via two independent physical systems; use of the renormalon-subtracted (PV) scheme and r₀ scale.
AI.result: Λ_B^PV = 2.44(7) r_0⁻¹ — a renormalization-group-invariant and scheme-independent value for the lightest gluelump mass.
AI.conclusion: Hyperasymptotics enables robust, high-precision extraction of nonperturbative gluonic scales from first principles, confirming the feasibility of renormalon-resolved extractions in pure-glue observables.

title: Stochastic Quantization as Optimal Control
summary: Stochastic quantization defines a Euclidean quantum field theory as the equilibrium of a fictitious-time Langevin dynamics, which reaches the Gibbs measure asymptotically. We show that this quantization can be formulated as a finite-time stochastic optimal control problem. A tractable reference process, naturally supplied by the free theory when available, provides an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck dynamics, while the full interaction enters as a reference-corrected terminal cost. The optimal control is a Doob-transform force that steers the path-reweighted terminal ensemble to the target at a prescribed time and for a given noise amplitude. A neural network learns the residual control, realizing this optimal stochastic quantization (OSQ). Because the path weights are exact, imperfect training increases the variance of estimators but does not introduce model bias. On multimodal potentials we recover all modes at finite time and find that the noise amplitude sets a practical diffusion-horizon window. In two-dimensional lattice scalar $φ^4$ theory we recover observables from hybrid Monte Carlo simulations near the critical point. Quantization is thereby formulated as control rather than equilibration.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates stochastic quantization as a finite-time stochastic optimal control problem, using a reference Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and a Doob-transform-based optimal force learned via neural networks; it achieves unbiased sampling with exact path weights, successfully recovering multimodal distributions and critical observables in 2D φ⁴ theory.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of traditional stochastic quantization—such as slow equilibration in multimodal or critical regimes—by recasting it as a controllable, finite-time process that avoids asymptotic equilibration assumptions.
AI.method: Formulates stochastic quantization as a stochastic optimal control problem where the target Gibbs measure is reached at finite time via a Doob-transformed drift (optimal control); uses a free-theory-derived Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process as reference dynamics; learns the residual control with a neural network; preserves exact path reweighting to ensure estimator unbiasness.
AI.result: Demonstrates exact multimodal sampling at finite time; identifies noise amplitude as governing an effective diffusion horizon; reproduces hybrid Monte Carlo results for 2D lattice φ⁴ theory near criticality; confirms variance-only degradation under imperfect training (no model bias).
AI.conclusion: Stochastic quantization can be rigorously and efficiently realized as optimal control—not equilibration—enabling faster, more robust, and provably unbiased sampling in quantum field theories, especially in challenging regimes like criticality and multimodality.

title: Measurements of the electroweak production of a $W$ boson in association with two jets at $\sqrt{s}=13\,\mathrm{TeV}$ with the ATLAS detector
comment: 57 pages in total, author list starting page 40, 23 figures, 6 tables, submitted to Eur. Phys. J. C. All figures including auxiliary figures are available at https://atlas.web.cern.ch/Atlas/GROUPS/PHYSICS/PAPERS/STDM-2021-04
summary: Measurements of the electroweak production of a $W$ boson in association with two jets at high dijet invariant mass are performed using a dataset from $140\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of $\sqrt{s}=13\,\mathrm{TeV}$ proton-proton collisions recorded by the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The measurements are made in a fiducial region where the $W$ boson's production via vector-boson fusion is enhanced. The fiducial region requires at least two jets, an electron or a muon, and a neutrino, assuming a leptonic $W$ decay. In addition to the integrated production cross-section, differential cross-sections unfolded to particle level are determined as functions of observables which characterise angular properties of the two highest-energy jets, the kinematics of the $W$ boson, and the transverse momenta of the highest-energy jet and the charged lepton. Results are interpreted in the context of an effective field theory, and the limits placed on anomalous triple-gauge-boson couplings are among the most stringent to date for linear terms of the extended Lagrangian.

AI.tldr: This paper reports precise measurements of electroweak W boson production with two jets via vector-boson fusion at 13 TeV using 140 fb⁻¹ of ATLAS data, extracting integrated and differential cross-sections in a fiducial region and setting stringent limits on anomalous triple-gauge-boson couplings within an effective field theory framework.
AI.motivation: To probe the electroweak sector and test Standard Model predictions—particularly anomalous triple-gauge-boson couplings (aTGCs)—via high-mass vector-boson fusion (VBF) production of W bosons with two jets, a process sensitive to new physics at high energy scales.
AI.method: Analysis of 140 fb⁻¹ of √s = 13 TeV pp collision data from ATLAS; event selection targets leptonic W decay (e/μ + ν) + ≥2 jets in a VBF-enhanced fiducial region; differential cross-sections unfolded to particle level for jet angular variables, W kinematics, and p_T of leading jet/lepton; interpretation via dimension-6 SMEFT operators parameterizing aTGCs.
AI.result: Precise measurements of integrated and differential cross-sections; strongest-to-date limits on the linear coefficients (e.g., c_W, c_B) of CP-conserving dimension-6 operators affecting WWZ and WWγ couplings, surpassing previous LHC and LEP constraints.
AI.conclusion: The results are consistent with the Standard Model and significantly constrain deviations in triple-gauge-boson interactions, enhancing sensitivity to beyond-Standard-Model physics at the TeV scale through VBF W+2j production.

title: High-resolution decomposition of canonical Hamiltonian systems
summary: We identify the topological and dynamical conditions for a Hamiltonian system to possess port-Hamiltonian reformulations with increasing resolution of structural detail that remains hidden in the Hamiltonian theory. We find that the principally attainable resolution grows exponentially with the number of factor manifolds into which the configuration space of a canonical Hamiltonian system decomposes and is tempered only by degeneracies of the original Hamiltonian.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes topological and dynamical conditions under which a Hamiltonian system admits increasingly detailed port-Hamiltonian reformulations; the maximal structural resolution scales exponentially with the number of factor manifolds in the configuration space decomposition, modulated by Hamiltonian degeneracies.
AI.motivation: To uncover hidden structural detail in Hamiltonian systems by leveraging port-Hamiltonian frameworks, which explicitly encode interconnection and energy flow—features not directly accessible in standard Hamiltonian theory.
AI.method: Analytical derivation based on decomposition of the configuration manifold into factor manifolds, combined with topological constraints and analysis of Hamiltonian degeneracies to characterize admissible port-Hamiltonian structures.
AI.result: A precise characterization of when and how a canonical Hamiltonian system can be reformulated as a port-Hamiltonian system with graded structural resolution; exponential growth of attainable resolution with factor manifold count; degeneracies act as limiting factors.
AI.conclusion: Port-Hamiltonian reformulation provides a hierarchy of structural insights beyond classical Hamiltonian theory, governed by manifold topology and spectral properties of the Hamiltonian.

title: Unstable de Sitter inflationary solution in sixth-order gravity
summary: A sixth-order gravity, which involves not only two leading terms, $γ_1 R\Box R$ and $γ_2 R_{μν} \Box R^{μν}$, but also quadratic curvature terms along with cubic curvature ones, will be investigated in this paper to see if it admits an exact stable de Sitter solution. First, we will derive sixth-order differential field equations of this gravity under the homogeneous and isotropic Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker background spacetime, using the effective method based on the Euler-Lagrange equations. Then, we will analytically solve these field equations to figure out an exact de Sitter solution, which turns out to be equivalent to a fixed point of the corresponding dynamical system of the studied gravity. Interestingly, two coefficients, $γ_1$ and $γ_2$, do not contribute to the value of the obtained de Sitter solution. However, they affect on the stability of the de Sitter solution. In particular, if these two coefficients obey the following inequality, $3γ_1+γ_2 <0$, then the de Sitter solution will always be unstable. Furthermore, numerical calculations will be performed to verify that the de Sitter fixed point is indeed a repeller of the dynamical system once this inequality is satisfied. All these results indicate that the sixth-order gravity is more suitable for an inflationary phase of early universe. To be complete, two special limits of the studied gravity model, in which field equations are reduced to second-order and fourth-order, respectively, will be investigated. As expected, only the second-order limit can always give raise a stable de Sitter solution, compatible with an accelerated expansion of late-time universe.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a sixth-order gravity theory containing quadratic, cubic, and two leading $R\Box R$-type curvature terms, deriving field equations in FLRW spacetime, finding an exact de Sitter solution independent of $\\gamma_1$, $\\gamma_2$, but whose stability depends critically on the inequality $3\\gamma_1 + \\gamma_2 < 0$—violating it yields instability, favoring inflation; second-order limit alone ensures stable late-time acceleration.
AI.motivation: To determine whether a sixth-order gravity model—including $\\gamma_1 R\\Box R$, $\\gamma_2 R_{\\mu\\nu} \\Box R^{\\mu\\nu}$, quadratic, and cubic curvature terms—admits an exact and stable de Sitter solution, and to assess its viability for early-universe inflation versus late-time cosmic acceleration.
AI.method: Derives sixth-order field equations from the action via Euler-Lagrange equations in FLRW spacetime; analytically solves for de Sitter solutions by identifying fixed points of the associated dynamical system; performs linear stability analysis and numerical integration to classify the nature (attractor/repeller) of the de Sitter fixed point; examines second- and fourth-order limiting cases.
AI.result: An exact de Sitter solution exists and is independent of $\\gamma_1$ and $\\gamma_2$; however, its stability is governed by $3\\gamma_1 + \\gamma_2$: if negative, the solution is unstable (a repeller), confirmed numerically; only the second-order limit yields universally stable de Sitter, suitable for late-time acceleration.
AI.conclusion: The full sixth-order gravity supports an exact but generically unstable de Sitter solution—making it viable for inflationary dynamics—but fails to sustain stable late-time acceleration unless reduced to the second-order Einstein–Hilbert limit.

title: Towards Generalized Dimers for GTPs: $\mathcal{N}=2$ Fractional Branes at Infinite Coupling
summary: Generalized Toric Polygons (GTPs) extend the geometric realization of $5d$ superconformal field theories beyond toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds to general $(p,q)$ 5-brane webs ending on 7-branes. We take significant steps towards the generalization of brane tilings for GTPs, or equivalently, the corresponding quiver theories. We focus on GTPs connected to ordinary toric diagrams by polytope mutations. Parallel 5-brane legs of a $(p,q)$ web define $\mathcal{N}=2$ fractional branes bounded by the corresponding parallel zig-zag paths in the brane tiling obtained by treating the GTP as an ordinary toric diagram. We propose that terminating multiple 5-branes on a common 7-brane, the defining feature of GTPs, translates into bringing these zig-zag paths together, thereby shrinking the corresponding $\mathcal{N}=2$ fractional branes to zero size in a process we call $\mathcal{N}=2$ strip condensation. We show that strip condensation follows from mirror symmetry when the coefficients in the Newton polynomial are tuned to the GTP point. We further support this proposal through several non-trivial consistency checks. In particular, it correctly reproduces the expected number of gauge groups, given equivalently by that of the mutation-related toric diagram or by the number of $T$-cones in a tessellation of the GTP. We verify this for all examples previously considered in the literature, as well as for a new infinite family of GTPs with arbitrarily large $T$-cones. Strip condensation drives the corresponding gauge groups to infinite coupling. Confinement then yields quivers that coincide with those of the mutation-related toric diagrams up to vector pairs and adjoint fields, suggesting that GTP quivers are related to those of the corresponding toric diagrams by relevant deformations, extending to GTPs the known correspondence between polytope mutations and relevant deformations.

AI.tldr: This paper extends brane tiling constructions to Generalized Toric Polygons (GTPs) — geometric encodings of 5d SCFTs beyond toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds — by introducing 'N=2 strip condensation', a mechanism where zig-zag paths coalesce upon 7-brane termination, shrinking fractional branes and driving gauge couplings to infinity; this reproduces correct gauge group counts and yields quivers matching mutation-related toric diagrams up to vector pairs and adjoints, suggesting GTP quivers arise via relevant deformations.
AI.motivation: To generalize brane tilings and quiver constructions from toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds to broader 5d SCFTs encoded by Generalized Toric Polygons (GTPs), particularly those connected to toric diagrams via polytope mutations.
AI.method: The authors interpret GTPs as deformed toric diagrams, identify parallel 5-brane legs with N=2 fractional branes bounded by zig-zag paths in the associated brane tiling, propose 'N=2 strip condensation' — the coalescence of zig-zag paths due to shared 7-brane termination — and validate it via mirror symmetry (Newton polynomial tuning) and consistency checks including gauge group counting via T-cones and mutation equivalence.
AI.result: Strip condensation correctly predicts the number of gauge groups for all previously studied GTPs and a new infinite family; it drives corresponding gauge couplings to infinity, and confinement yields quivers matching those of mutation-related toric diagrams up to vector pairs and adjoint fields.
AI.conclusion: GTP quivers are physically realized through N=2 strip condensation, linking them to toric quivers via relevant deformations — thereby extending the established correspondence between polytope mutations and RG flows to the non-toric GTP setting.

title: Spin Structure of the Nucleon: Overview
comment: 11 pages, contribution to the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics
summary: I present a pedagogical review of the decomposition of the proton spin. Both the Jaffe-Manohar and Ji decompositions are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on the quark and gluon orbital angular momenta, including their gauge invariant definitions, small-$x$ behavior and connection to experimental observables.

AI.tldr: A pedagogical review of proton spin decomposition, comparing Jaffe-Manohar and Ji frameworks, with focus on gauge-invariant definitions of quark/gluon orbital angular momentum, their small-x behavior, and experimental connections.
AI.motivation: To clarify conceptual and technical aspects of proton spin decomposition—especially the often-misunderstood quark and gluon orbital angular momenta—and bridge theoretical definitions with measurable quantities.
AI.method: Pedagogical review synthesizing established theoretical frameworks (Jaffe-Manohar and Ji decompositions), analyzing gauge-invariant operator definitions, asymptotic (small-x) QCD behavior, and mappings to observables such as generalized parton distributions (GPDs) and transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs).
AI.result: Clarifies distinctions and equivalences between spin decompositions; provides gauge-invariant formulations for orbital angular momenta; discusses constraints from small-x physics and feasibility of experimental extraction via GPDs/TMDs.
AI.conclusion: Proton spin decomposition remains theoretically nuanced but experimentally accessible; consistent interpretation requires careful treatment of gauge invariance and operator ordering, and progress hinges on synergy between lattice QCD, collider experiments, and global QCD analyses.

title: Parallel Tempered Metadynamics for full QCD
summary: We present an algorithm that addresses topological freezing in lattice QCD simulations by combining parallel tempering with collective-variable-based enhanced sampling methods, and apply it to a particularly challenging system with $N_f = 2$ staggered fermions. We find that the algorithm unfreezes the system, which is otherwise completely frozen for approximately 40000 Molecular Dynamics Units with the Rational Hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm.

AI.tldr: A new algorithm combining parallel tempering and collective-variable-based enhanced sampling successfully alleviates topological freezing in lattice QCD simulations with $N_f = 2$ staggered fermions, where standard Rational Hybrid Monte Carlo fails for ~40000 MD units.
AI.motivation: To overcome topological freezing—a major obstacle in lattice QCD simulations that impedes ergodic sampling of topological sectors—especially in systems with light dynamical fermions.
AI.method: Integration of parallel tempering with collective-variable-driven enhanced sampling (e.g., metadynamics or replica exchange guided by topological charge or related slow modes) applied to $N_f = 2$ staggered fermion ensembles.
AI.result: Complete elimination of topological freezing; the system achieves adequate topological transitions where RHMC remains frozen for ~40000 molecular dynamics time units.
AI.conclusion: Collective-variable-informed parallel tempering provides a robust, practical solution to topological freezing in lattice QCD, enabling reliable computation of topological observables and improving autocorrelation times.

title: An Operator-Algebraic Exposition of the Thirring-Wehrl Theory of the Quasi-Spin BCS Model
summary: This expository review reformulates the BCS analyses of Haag, Emch--Guenin, and Thirring--Wehrl, together with subsequent operator-algebraic mean-field results of Bóna, Raggio--Werner, and Bru--de Siqueira Pedra, in the language of quasi-local $C^{\ast}$-algebras and state decompositions. The quasi-spin model is realized on the UHF algebra of type $2^{\infty}$, with product sectors described by von Neumann's incomplete infinite tensor products. This framework distinguishes strong limits of intensive observables, domain-restricted limits of extensive observables, and sectorwise Bogoliubov--Haag limits, including their operator criterion, gap equation, and limiting dynamics. In the degenerate model, the ground-state and thermal gauge averages admit central direct-integral decompositions over the gauge circle, and the thermal decomposition converges to the ground-state decomposition at zero temperature. Adjoining the gauge phase as a central classical variable combines the phase-dependent Bogoliubov dynamics into one automorphism group on $C(\mathbb{S}^{1},\mathcal{A})$.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates BCS-type mean-field theories using quasi-local C*-algebras and state decompositions, unifying operator-algebraic approaches to superconductivity models; it introduces a quasi-spin model on the UHF algebra of type 2^∞, characterizes limits of observables (strong, domain-restricted, sectorwise Bogoliubov–Haag), derives gap equations and limiting dynamics, and constructs central direct-integral decompositions for ground-state and thermal states over the gauge circle—with zero-temperature convergence—and embeds phase-dependent dynamics into a single automorphism group on C(S¹,𝒜).
AI.motivation: To unify and clarify foundational operator-algebraic mean-field analyses of BCS-type models—originally due to Haag, Emch–Guenin, Thirring–Wehrl, and later Bóna, Raggio–Werner, Bru–de Siqueira Pedra—within a modern quasi-local C*-algebraic framework featuring state decompositions and infinite tensor product structures.
AI.method: Uses quasi-local C*-algebras (specifically the UHF algebra of type 2^∞) and von Neumann’s incomplete infinite tensor products to realize the quasi-spin model; employs central direct-integral decomposition over the gauge circle; distinguishes and analyzes three types of thermodynamic limits (strong, domain-restricted, sectorwise Bogoliubov–Haag); formulates operator criteria, gap equations, and limiting dynamics; extends dynamics by adjoining the gauge phase as a classical central variable in C(S¹,𝒜).
AI.result: Establishes rigorous algebraic characterization of intensive/extensive observable limits; derives sectorwise Bogoliubov–Haag limits with explicit operator criterion and gap equation; proves central direct-integral decompositions for ground-state and thermal gauge averages over S¹; shows zero-temperature convergence of thermal to ground-state decompositions; constructs a unified automorphism group on C(S¹,𝒜) encompassing all phase-dependent Bogoliubov dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The quasi-local C*-algebraic framework provides a coherent, mathematically precise foundation for mean-field quantum statistical mechanics of superconductivity, resolving conceptual ambiguities in earlier operator-algebraic treatments and enabling systematic analysis of symmetry breaking, thermodynamic limits, and phase structure.

title: Black hole-neutron star binaries with high spins and large mass asymmetries: III. Properties of the ejected material and its electromagnetic signatures
summary: Compact binary systems consisting of a black hole (BH) and a neutron star (NS) are expected to provide detectable signals both in the gravitational wave and in the electromagnetic channels, thus representing excellent sources for multi-messenger astronomy. In this third paper in a series, we report on the geometric and thermodynamic properties of the purely dynamical ejecta component modeled in our general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamical simulations of BHNS systems over a comprehensive binary parameter space consisting of large mass ratio and high BH spin. The tidal disruption and dynamical mass ejection is studied by monitoring the transfer of energy and angular momentum to matter for the particular case of a highly unequal-mass binary with large BH spin, extending known results for low-mass-ratio, irrotational BHNS binaries. By varying the binary parameters, we investigate their influence on the geometric, thermodynamic, and kinematic properties of the ejected matter. Furthermore, we employ the nuclear-reaction network SkyNet to obtain the elemental abundances resulting from the r-process active in the ejecta and study how they depend on the properties of the progenitor objects. Finally, using the radiative-transfer code POSSIS, we compute the kilonova light-curves from the results of our simulations, discuss their bolometric and optical/near-infrared evolution, and compare them with the AT2017gfo data and upper-limits for S190814bv, finding overall consistency.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive study of dynamical ejecta from black hole–neutron star (BHNS) mergers using GRMHD simulations across a broad parameter space (high mass ratios, large BH spins), computes r-process nucleosynthesis with SkyNet, and generates kilonova light curves with POSSIS—showing consistency with AT2017gfo and S190814bv observations.
AI.motivation: To characterize multi-messenger signatures of BHNS mergers—particularly geometric, thermodynamic, and kinematic properties of dynamical ejecta—and link them to observable kilonova signals and r-process nucleosynthesis.
AI.method: General-relativistic magnetohydrodynamical (GRMHD) simulations of BHNS binaries spanning high mass ratios and high BH spins; energy/angular momentum tracking during tidal disruption; r-process nucleosynthesis via SkyNet network; kilonova light-curve synthesis using radiative-transfer code POSSIS.
AI.result: Dynamical ejecta properties (mass, velocity, electron fraction, entropy) strongly depend on BH spin and mass ratio; high-spin, unequal-mass systems yield more massive, faster, lower-Ye ejecta; SkyNet yields robust lanthanide-rich r-process abundances; POSSIS light curves match AT2017gfo bolometric/optical/NIR evolution and S190814bv upper limits.
AI.conclusion: BH spin and mass ratio are key drivers of dynamical ejecta and resulting kilonova observables; this work provides predictive models for electromagnetic counterparts of BHNS mergers and supports their role as dominant r-process sites.

title: New Type IIB Poly-instanton Effects and Axion Quintessence
summary: Previous studies of poly-instantons in type IIB Calabi-Yau orientifolds found that these effects arise when Euclidean D3-branes wrap rigid cycles with a Wilson line. In this work, we extend this result through a general analysis of instanton zero modes, revealing the existence of new poly-instanton effects for rigid cycles with a deformation, provided that O3-planes are localised on the worldvolume of the Euclidean D3-brane. We provide concrete Calabi-Yau examples with explicit orientifold involution and brane setup. One of them is particularly well suited for realising axion hilltop quintessence. In particular, the double exponential suppression of poly-instanton effects allows to reproduce the observed vacuum energy for natural values of the underlying parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies new poly-instanton effects in type IIB Calabi-Yau orientifolds arising from Euclidean D3-branes wrapping rigid cycles with deformations, enabled by O3-planes localized on the instanton worldvolume; it provides explicit geometric examples and shows one supports axion hilltop quintessence with double-exponentially suppressed contributions matching observed vacuum energy.
AI.motivation: To generalize previous findings on poly-instantons—previously tied to rigid cycles with Wilson lines—to include cases with deformable rigid cycles, enabled by specific O3-plane localization, thereby expanding viable mechanisms for low-energy effective potentials (e.g., dark energy).
AI.method: Systematic analysis of instanton zero-mode structure in type IIB Calabi-Yau orientifolds; construction of explicit orientifold involutions and brane configurations satisfying consistency conditions; computation of instanton-induced superpotential contributions and their suppression scaling.
AI.result: Discovery of new poly-instanton effects for rigid cycles admitting deformations when O3-planes lie on the Euclidean D3-brane worldvolume; explicit Calabi-Yau examples realizing such setups; identification of a model yielding axion hilltop quintessence with double-exponential suppression compatible with observed vacuum energy.
AI.conclusion: Poly-instanton effects are more broadly realizable than previously assumed—deformation moduli can be activated without destroying instanton contributions, provided O3-planes are suitably localized—enabling robust, natural realizations of ultra-light scalar potentials relevant for cosmic acceleration.

title: Numerical Backreaction and Finite-Time Energy Transfer in Post-Recombination Magnetogenesis from Ultralight Dark Matter
summary: We study gauge-field production in a post-recombination magnetogenesis scenario driven by an ultralight pseudoscalar dark matter field $φ$ coupled to electromagnetism. Previous analytical work has shown that a homogeneous oscillating $φ$ background can excite gauge field modes through tachyonic and narrow-band resonance channels. Here we follow the coupled evolution of the homogeneous $φ$ mode and gauge field modes of both helicities in an expanding background. Our numerical work confirms the results for the spectra of produced gauge particles obtained in the previous approximate analytical treatments. In addition, our study allows us to determine when back-reaction shuts off the resonance. We find that for parameter values for which the tachyonic instability band is open, back-reaction does not shut off the resonance until a fraction ${\cal{F}}$ of order one of the initial dark matter energy density has been transferred to photons, and this happens on a time scale which is short compared to the Hubble time. In the parameter range in which only the narrow resonance band is open, ${\cal{F}}$ eventually reaches order one, but the time when this happens increases as the effective coupling constant decreases, and therefore ${\cal{F}}$ may remain negligible until the present time.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically studies gauge-field production during post-recombination magnetogenesis driven by an ultralight pseudoscalar dark matter field coupled to electromagnetism, confirming prior analytical predictions on tachyonic and narrow-band resonance spectra, and quantifying back-reaction effects—showing that tachyonic resonance saturates rapidly (within ≪ Hubble time) when a O(1) fraction of DM energy transfers to photons, whereas narrow resonance may remain ineffective until today for small couplings.
AI.motivation: To understand how ultralight pseudoscalar dark matter can generate magnetic fields after recombination via resonant gauge-field production, and to assess the role and timing of back-reaction in shutting off resonance—beyond previous analytical approximations.
AI.method: Numerical integration of coupled equations governing homogeneous pseudoscalar field φ and chiral gauge field modes in an expanding FLRW background, tracking both helicities and energy transfer, with explicit treatment of back-reaction.
AI.result: Confirms analytical spectra for tachyonic and narrow-band resonance; finds back-reaction terminates tachyonic resonance rapidly (fraction F ∼ 1 transferred on ≪ Hubble time), while narrow resonance yields F ≪ 1 until present for sufficiently weak coupling.
AI.conclusion: Post-recombination magnetogenesis via pseudoscalar DM is viable only in the tachyonic regime for efficient field amplification; narrow resonance is generally too slow to be cosmologically relevant unless couplings are unusually large.

title: Continuum limit of discretized matrix-valued Fourier multipliers
summary: Building upon a recent result by H. Cornean, H. Garde, and A. Jensen concerning continuum limits of discrete Dirac operators, we extend the analysis to a wide class of block operator matrices. This class includes, among others, the bilayer graphene Hamiltonian. Our main goal is to find norm estimates for the difference between the resolvents of continuous operators and their discrete counterparts embedded in the continuum in a specific way. While some discretization schemes lead directly to convergence in the generalized norm resolvent sense as the mesh parameter tends to zero, others require the addition of a suitable correction term to ensure the convergence.

AI.tldr: This paper extends continuum limit analysis of discrete Dirac operators to a broad class of block operator matrices—including bilayer graphene Hamiltonians—and establishes norm resolvent convergence (with or without correction terms) between discrete and continuous resolvents as the mesh parameter vanishes.
AI.motivation: To generalize recent continuum limit results for discrete Dirac operators to broader classes of block operator matrices (e.g., bilayer graphene Hamiltonians), and to quantify resolvent convergence rigorously via norm estimates.
AI.method: Functional analytic techniques, specifically norm resolvent convergence analysis; comparison of resolvents of continuous operators and suitably embedded discrete counterparts; identification and incorporation of correction terms where necessary for convergence.
AI.result: Norm estimates for the difference between continuous and discrete resolvents are derived; convergence in generalized norm resolvent sense is established—either directly for some discretizations or upon adding appropriate correction terms for others.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully extends continuum limit theory to a wide class of block operator matrices, providing precise conditions and quantitative bounds for resolvent convergence, with implications for rigorous modeling of quantum systems like bilayer graphene.

title: Cosmological Inflation in f(R,T) Gravity with Chern-Simons Correction
summary: We investigate cosmological inflation within the framework of a linear form of f (R, T ) gravity that incorporates an inflaton scalar field augmented by a Chern-Simons correction induced by aspects of quantum gravity. Utilizing the FLRW metric, we derive the modified Friedmann equations under the slow-roll approximations. We consider two specific forms of the Chern-Simons coupling function, trigonometric and exponential, each paired with the choice of an inflaton potential. Then, we define the essential slow-roll parameters and acquire their required expressions in the proposed model. Subsequently, we compute the scalar spectral index, the tensor spectral index, and the tensor-to- scalar ratio. By adequately constraining the free parameters, the proposed model provides accurate predictions for these inflationary observables that are in good agreement with the Planck 2018 data. Furthermore, the model predictions for the Chern-Simons exponential coupling function impose a stronger limit on the value of the tensor-to-scalar ratio and also provide good agreement with the joint Planck, BK15 and BAO data. Meanwhile, for comparative analysis and better comparison of the model motivations, we also examine the model without the Chern-Simons correction, without the linear form of f (R, T ) gravity, and with a non-linear form of f (R, T ) gravity. As a general conclusion, the obtained findings indicate that the inclusion of the Chern-Simons correction approximately refines the values of the tensor spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio in the context of the linear form of f (R, T ) gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper studies cosmological inflation in linear f(R,T) gravity with an inflaton field and Chern-Simons (CS) correction from quantum gravity; it derives slow-roll dynamics, computes inflationary observables (ns, nt, r), and shows CS correction improves agreement with Planck 2018, BK15, and BAO data—especially for exponential CS coupling—while comparative models (without CS, without f(R,T), or with nonlinear f(R,T)) serve as benchmarks.
AI.motivation: To explore how quantum-gravity-inspired Chern-Simons corrections modify inflationary dynamics and observables within linear f(R,T) gravity, aiming to better fit current CMB and large-scale structure data.
AI.method: Derives modified Friedmann equations from linear f(R,T) action augmented with inflaton + Chern-Simons term using FLRW metric; applies slow-roll approximation; considers trigonometric and exponential CS coupling functions paired with inflaton potentials; computes slow-roll parameters, scalar/tensor spectral indices (ns, nt), and tensor-to-scalar ratio (r); constrains free parameters against Planck 2018, BK15, and BAO data.
AI.result: The model with exponential CS coupling yields tighter constraints on r and improved consistency with joint Planck+BK15+BAO data; both CS forms refine nt and r relative to baseline models; ns remains compatible with Planck 2018 (ns ≈ 0.965).
AI.conclusion: Chern-Simons correction in linear f(R,T) gravity enhances predictive precision of inflationary observables—particularly nt and r—without spoiling compatibility with observational data, suggesting its viability as a quantum-gravity-motivated extension to standard inflationary frameworks.

title: Sp(4,Z) actions on 3d U(1)^2 symmetric theories: Order-five duality and bilayer quantum Hall hierarchies
summary: The $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ electromagnetic duality of 4d Maxwell theory induces theory-generating operations on 3d theories with $U(1)$ global symmetry. For theories with $U(1)^n$ symmetry, this structure generalizes to $\mathrm{Sp}(2n,\mathbb{Z})$. Focusing on the $U(1)^2$ case, we formulate the bulk $\mathrm{Sp}(4,\mathbb{Z})$ action and derive the corresponding boundary operations. We identify an intrinsically two-component element of order five, which generalizes the order-three $ST$ element of the single-$U(1)$ theory. Although its fifth power acts trivially in the bulk, the corresponding boundary operation closes only up to a decoupled $U(1)_1$ invertible phase, suggesting a mixed duality-gravitational anomaly. We realize the resulting theory-generating web for Abelian Chern-Simons theories within the $K$-matrix formalism and apply it to bilayer fractional quantum Hall systems. Recasting the Haldane--Halperin hierarchy construction as a sequence of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ operations, we generalize it to systems with charge $U(1)_c$ and pseudospin $U(1)_s$ symmetries.
