The resulting bilayer hierarchies contain branches terminating in an interlayer-correlated bosonic $(221)$ daughter sector, yielding candidate Abelian states at the even-denominator equal-layer fillings $3/8+3/8$ and $5/12+5/12$. Integral changes of anyon basis establish the equivalence of these states to their corresponding Abelian composite-fermion descriptions. We further discuss the spin-charge constraints that arise when the electromagnetic background field is treated as a spin-$c$ connection.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes electromagnetic duality from SL(2,Z) in single-U(1) 4d Maxwell theory to Sp(4,Z) for U(1)^2-symmetric 3d boundary theories; identifies a novel order-five boundary duality operation with mixed duality-gravitational anomaly; applies the formalism to bilayer FQH systems, generating new Abelian candidate states at even-denominator fillings (e.g., 3/8+3/8, 5/12+5/12) and establishing their equivalence to composite-fermion descriptions via K-matrix transformations.
AI.motivation: To extend electromagnetic duality beyond single-U(1) systems and systematically generate new topological phases—especially at experimentally relevant even-denominator fillings—in bilayer fractional quantum Hall systems using higher-rank duality groups.
AI.method: Uses bulk-boundary correspondence for 4d Maxwell theory with U(1)^2 global symmetry; constructs Sp(4,Z) duality action on 3d boundary theories; employs K-matrix formalism for Abelian Chern-Simons theories; implements integral basis changes (GL(2,Z) transformations) to establish phase equivalences; incorporates spin-charge coupling via spin-c connection for electromagnetic background.
AI.result: Identifies an intrinsically two-component Sp(4,Z) element of order five whose boundary action closes only up to a decoupled U(1)_1 invertible phase—signaling a mixed duality-gravitational anomaly; constructs new Abelian bilayer FQH states at fillings 3/8+3/8 and 5/12+5/12 terminating in interlayer-correlated (221) sector; proves equivalence to composite-fermion descriptions via K-matrix isomorphisms; derives spin-charge constraints under spin-c connection.
AI.conclusion: Sp(2n,Z) duality provides a powerful framework for generating and classifying multi-component topological orders; the discovered order-five operation reveals novel anomaly structures; the resulting bilayer hierarchies offer concrete, anomaly-consistent Abelian candidates for even-denominator FQH physics.

title: The supernumerary $K(1690)$ signal from COMPASS as a strange hybrid state
comment: 7 pages, 1 figures, 5 tables. Comments are welcome
summary: The $K(1690)$ state with $J^P=0^-$ was recently discovered by the COMPASS Collaboration in the scattering reaction $K^-+p\to K^-π^-π^++p$, leading to three observed pseudoscalar strange mesons, namely the $K(1460)$, $K(1690)$, and $K(1830)$, in the 1.0$-$2.0 GeV region. However, within the quark model, only the $2^1S_0$ and $3^1S_0$ strange meson states are expected in this energy region. Therefore, at least one of these states should be interpreted as an exotic candidate. In this work, we study the spectrum of strange mesons systematically, and find that the $K(1460)$ and $K(1830)$ are good candidates of $2^1S_0$ and $3^1S_0$ strange mesons, respectively. A further investigation of their strong decays also supports this assignment. Furthermore, we note that the production mechanism of the $K(1690)$ is similar to that of the $π_1(1600)$, which has been widely regarded as a hybrid meson candidate. We investigate the strong decays of the $K(1690)$ within a constituent gluon model by treating it as a $0^-$ strange hybrid meson and find that the results support the $K(1690)$ as a hybrid state. Finally, we identify several important decay modes of the $K(1690)$ that may be used in future experiments to test whether it contains the $n^1S_0$ ($n=$2 and 3) $s\bar{q}$ component. We also suggest BESIII to search for the $K(1690)$ state through the $J/ψ\to K K(1690) \to KK^{\ast}_0(1430)π\to KKππ$ process.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the newly observed K(1690) meson with J^P=0^- and proposes it as a hybrid meson candidate, distinguishing it from conventional quark-model states K(1460) and K(1830), which are assigned as 2^1S_0 and 3^1S_0 s\bar{q} states; strong decay analyses within a constituent gluon model support the hybrid interpretation, and specific experimental channels (e.g., J/ψ→KK(1690)→KKππ) are suggested for verification.
AI.motivation: The observation of three strange mesons (K(1460), K(1690), K(1830)) in the 1.0–2.0 GeV region contradicts quark model expectations—only two s\bar{q} S-wave states (2^1S_0 and 3^1S_0) are predicted—necessitating identification of at least one exotic (non-qq̄) state; K(1690)'s production similarity to the hybrid candidate π₁(1600) motivates its hybrid interpretation.
AI.method: Systematic spectrum analysis and strong decay calculations using the constituent gluon model (CGM), treating K(1690) as a 0^- strange hybrid meson (s\bar{q}g); assignments of K(1460) and K(1830) are validated via mass and decay patterns consistent with 2^1S_0 and 3^1S_0 quark-model states.
AI.result: K(1460) and K(1830) are confirmed as likely 2^1S_0 and 3^1S_0 s\bar{q} states; K(1690)’s decay properties (e.g., dominant Kη, Kη′, K*π modes) are quantitatively consistent with a 0^- hybrid assignment in CGM; key testable decay modes identified, and a dedicated search channel J/ψ→KK(1690)→KKππ is proposed for BESIII.
AI.conclusion: K(1690) is strongly supported as a strange hybrid meson (s\bar{q}g) with J^P=0^-, resolving the spectroscopic excess in the 1–2 GeV strange meson sector; this provides compelling evidence for gluonic excitations in the strange sector and motivates further experimental confirmation.

title: Transverse-momentum resummation effects on angular coefficients in Z and W boson hadroproduction
summary: We present a comprehensive analysis of the angular coefficients of $Z$ and $W$ boson production at hadron colliders in different kinematical ranges, using data from the ATLAS, LHCb, and CMS Collaborations at the LHC, as well as CDF data at the Tevatron. We provide theoretical predictions obtained by consistently combining the resummation of logarithmically enhanced QCD corrections at small transverse momenta $q_T$ up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy (NNLL) with fixed-order calculations at next-to-leading order (NLO), valid at large $q_T$. We quantify the impact of transverse-momentum resummation on the angular coefficients. We find that the inclusion of resummation effects leads to a moderate and systematic improvement in the description of the data in the intermediate $q_T$ region, $q_T \sim 20-50$~GeV, for several angular coefficients, while in the remaining cases it does not degrade the agreement of fixed-order QCD predictions with experimental measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes angular coefficients of Z and W boson production at hadron colliders, combining NNLL resummation at small q_T with NLO fixed-order calculations at large q_T, and assesses the impact of resummation on data description—showing moderate improvement in the intermediate q_T (20–50 GeV) region.
AI.motivation: To quantify the impact of transverse-momentum (q_T) resummation on angular coefficients of electroweak boson production, bridging theoretical precision across kinematic regimes and improving agreement with experimental data.
AI.method: Consistent combination of q_T resummation at NNLL accuracy (for small q_T) with NLO fixed-order QCD calculations (for large q_T), applied to angular coefficients measured by ATLAS, LHCb, CMS (LHC) and CDF (Tevatron).
AI.result: Resummation yields moderate, systematic improvement in describing several angular coefficients in the intermediate q_T region (~20–50 GeV); elsewhere, it preserves or does not worsen agreement with data compared to pure NLO predictions.
AI.conclusion: Transverse-momentum resummation enhances theoretical description of angular coefficients in the intermediate q_T regime without compromising agreement elsewhere, validating the hybrid NNLL+NLO approach for precision electroweak boson studies.

title: Charged Higgs Search at Future Neutrino Telescope and Higgs Factory
summary: We investigate the discovery potential of the charged Higgs boson at future lepton colliders and neutrino telescopes within two simplified benchmark scenarios with universal Yukawa couplings. We demonstrate that both the muon-track and cascade events at neutrino telescopes can be exploited to search for or constrain the charged Higgs boson through resonant neutrino scattering process, and we compare the sensitivities obtained under different astrophysical neutrino flux models. We study the effect of the detector volume of neutrino telescopes on the discovery potential of the charged Higgs boson. We study the signal of charged Higgs boson at future lepton colliders over different kinematic regimes using optimized reconstruction strategies. We compare the discovery potential of the two experimental approaches over the relevant parameter space and find that future lepton colliders generally provide better sensitivity in most of the parameter space, while neutrino telescopes with very large detector volume can offer competitive and complementary sensitivity in the heavy-mass region of the charged Higgs boson.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the discovery potential of the charged Higgs boson at future lepton colliders and neutrino telescopes using two universal-Yukawa benchmark scenarios; it finds lepton colliders generally superior, but large-volume neutrino telescopes competitive for heavy masses.
AI.motivation: To explore complementary probes of the charged Higgs boson beyond conventional collider searches, leveraging high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and precision lepton collider physics.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological analysis of resonant neutrino scattering (muon-track and cascade events) at neutrino telescopes under varying flux models and detector volumes; event simulation and optimized reconstruction of charged Higgs signals at future lepton colliders across kinematic regimes.
AI.result: Lepton colliders achieve better sensitivity over most parameter space; neutrino telescopes with very large volumes provide competitive, complementary reach for heavy charged Higgs masses (>1 TeV), depending on astrophysical neutrino flux assumptions.
AI.conclusion: Combined use of lepton colliders and next-generation neutrino telescopes enhances coverage of the charged Higgs parameter space, especially in high-mass regions inaccessible to colliders alone.

title: Representation of the causal logic for the Dirac system and the electron
summary: We construct a covariant representation of the causal logic for the Dirac system and the electron, based on the conserved Dirac probability current and a general current-to-localization procedure for achronal regions. A polynomial decay estimate, derived by a non-stationary phase argument, verifies the conditions required to define covariant achronal localization for the full Dirac system. Extending this localization to complete spacetime regions yields the corresponding causal-logic representation; restriction to the positive-energy invariant subspace gives the analogous construction for the electron. We establish several structural properties. On Euclidean space, Dirac localization agrees with canonical projection-valued localization, while its position operator differs from the Newton--Wigner operator by an explicitly determined bounded self-adjoint correction. Full Dirac achronal localization is projection valued and represents achronal separateness by orthogonality, thus satisfying microscopic causality. After compression to the electron subspace, it becomes positive-operator valued while preserving causality. We further extend known results from spatial to general achronal regions, prove separation and norm-one criteria, and analyze the high-boost limit, obtaining Lorentz contraction in a precise probabilistic sense. Finally, we discuss the electron--positron decomposition and the state transformation induced by position measurements, showing that measurement-induced positron production is universal and independent of the specific measuring device.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a covariant, causal-logic-based localization framework for the Dirac system and electron using conserved probability current and achronal regions; proves projection-valued (full Dirac) and POVM (electron-only) representations satisfying microscopic causality; establishes structural equivalence with canonical localization on Euclidean space, derives bounded correction to Newton–Wigner position operator; extends results to general achronal regions; demonstrates Lorentz contraction in measurement statistics; and proves universal, device-independent positron production upon position measurement.
AI.motivation: To resolve longstanding issues in relativistic quantum localization—namely, reconciling causality, covariance, and operational interpretability—by constructing a physically grounded, mathematically rigorous representation of causal logic for the Dirac system and its electron subspace.
AI.method: Covariant achronal localization built from the conserved Dirac probability current via a current-to-localization mapping; non-stationary phase analysis for polynomial decay estimates ensuring well-definedness; restriction to positive-energy subspace for electron-specific construction; spectral and operator-theoretic analysis to establish projection-valued/POVM nature, orthogonality/separateness, Lorentz behavior, and measurement-induced dynamics.
AI.result: A fully covariant, causally consistent localization scheme for the Dirac field: projection-valued for the full system (satisfying microscopic causality), POVM-valued for electrons alone (preserving causality); explicit bounded correction between Dirac and Newton–Wigner position operators; rigorous extension to arbitrary achronal regions; proven Lorentz contraction in high-boost limit; and proof that any ideal position measurement necessarily produces positrons with fixed, device-independent probability distribution.
AI.conclusion: The constructed causal-logic representation provides a consistent, operational, and relativistically invariant framework for localization in quantum field theory—resolving ambiguities in single-particle interpretations, unifying spatial and achronal localization, and revealing intrinsic entanglement between electron and positron degrees of freedom under measurement.

title: A product template bank to search for compact binary coalescences microlensed by isolated point mass lenses
summary: Gravitational waves (GW) from stellar mass compact binary coalescences (CBCs) that encounter a lens whose Schwarzschild radius is comparable to the GW wavelength, will be microlensed, leading to frequency-dependent modulations in the observed signal. Neglecting such wave-optics effects in standard templated searches for CBCs can result in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) losses as large as 30%. Here, we present a prescription for constructing a template bank targeted at microlensed GWs. We consider CBCs microlensed by isolated point mass lenses, whose frequency-dependent amplification factor is known to have a closed-form analytical expression. However, to construct the template bank, it suffices to use the geometric optics approximation, effectively modeling the microlensed signal as overlapping signals. Moreover, given that matched filtering is mostly sensitive to the phase of the GW signal, we use the phase of the amplification factor to compute the metric elements. The usual CBC parameter space is appended by two extra parameters: (i) the time-delay ($t_d$) between images and (ii) the relative-magnification ($μ_r$). By identifying the region of the lensing parameter space where the fitting factor (FF) falls below 97% due to wave-optics effects, we construct a template bank consisting of ~4000 templates covering the selected lensing region, independent of the values of the unlensed CBCs' parameters. We show that the bank targeting microlensed CBCs is, to a very good approximation, a Cartesian product of the unlensed CBC bank and the bank spanning the lensing parameters. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by evaluating fitting factors using both the unlensed CBC bank and the product template bank, finding a reduction of up to a factor of ~10 in the mismatch, as well as consistency with the prescribed minimal match criterion of 0.97 used in the construction of the banks.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a template bank for detecting microlensed gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences, incorporating two lensing parameters (time-delay and relative magnification) and achieving >97% fitting factor by accounting for wave-optics effects that cause up to 30% SNR loss in standard searches.
AI.motivation: Standard templated GW searches neglect wave-optics microlensing effects—when GW wavelength is comparable to lens Schwarzschild radius—causing up to 30% SNR loss; hence, a dedicated template bank is needed to recover such signals robustly.
AI.method: Constructs a geometric-optics-based template bank for point-mass microlensed CBCs, using only the phase of the analytical amplification factor to compute metric elements; extends the CBC parameter space with time-delay (t_d) and relative-magnification (μ_r); identifies lensing parameter region where fitting factor < 0.97 due to wave-optics deviations; builds ~4000-template bank as Cartesian product of unlensed CBC bank and lensing-parameter bank.
AI.result: The resulting microlensing-targeted bank achieves fitting factors ≥ 0.97 across the designated lensing region; mismatch reduction up to factor ~10 compared to unlensed bank; bank structure is approximately a Cartesian product; numerical validation confirms consistency with design criterion.
AI.conclusion: A computationally feasible, geometric-optics-inspired template bank incorporating two physically motivated lensing parameters suffices to detect microlensed CBCs with high fidelity, mitigating wave-optics-induced SNR losses without requiring full wave-optics templates.

title: Uniqueness of null-local modular flow
summary: In arXiv:2306.01837, it was conjectured that one can engineer a large class of quantum field theory states for which the modular flow on a spacelike slice is "instantaneously local." Here we show that on null slices, such flows are highly constrained; ultraviolet universality essentially requires null-local modular flow to be unique. Concretely, we study massless Klein-Gordon theory in Minkowski spacetime, and construct, for any sufficiently regular future-directed vector field on the past null boundary of a causal diamond, a state that has this vector field as its instantaneous modular flow. We then show by explicit computation that no two distinct states in this class can be realized in the same local Hilbert space. Using a more abstract argument, we also show that in the vacuum sector of the theory, the only null-local modular flow in a causal diamond is provided by the vacuum state itself. We also comment on the construction of null-local modular flow for massive scalars, free Maxwell fields, free gravitons, and in curved backgrounds.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that null-local modular flow in quantum field theory is highly constrained and essentially unique, showing that distinct states with different null modular flows cannot coexist in the same local Hilbert space—even for massless Klein-Gordon theory—and that only the vacuum state admits null-local modular flow in the vacuum sector of a causal diamond.
AI.motivation: To resolve the conjecture from arXiv:2306.01837 about instantaneously local modular flow by examining its feasibility and uniqueness on null slices, where UV universality imposes strong constraints.
AI.method: Explicit construction of states with prescribed future-directed vector fields as instantaneous modular flow on the past null boundary of a causal diamond in massless Klein-Gordon theory; direct computation of modular flow uniqueness; abstract algebraic argument using locality and vacuum sector structure.
AI.result: For massless scalar QFT in Minkowski space: (i) any sufficiently regular future-directed vector field on the past null boundary can be realized as instantaneous null modular flow of some state; (ii) no two such distinct states can be implemented in the same local Hilbert space; (iii) in the vacuum sector, only the vacuum state yields null-local modular flow in a causal diamond.
AI.conclusion: Null-local modular flow is not generic—it is rigid and essentially unique due to UV constraints; this contrasts sharply with spacelike modular flow and has implications for holography, entanglement structure, and state-dependent constructions in QFT.

title: Dark Monopoles, Bounds on Hidden Sectors, and Cosmological Implications
summary: Hidden sectors are a generic prediction of string theory compactifications and result in a promising landscape for dark matter model building. We consider the case of hidden sector magnetic monopoles produced via a thermal phase transition in the early Universe and subsequently diluted by pair annihilation. We show that for symmetry-breaking scales $\gtrsim 100\, \text{PeV}$, the monopole abundance is unacceptably high, overclosing the Universe. Our bounds are robust against variations in the initial fraction of energy density deposited in the hidden sector, exhibiting only a weak power-law dependence on this quantity. The bound is substantially tightened in the case of multiple hidden sectors. The standard cosmology may only be recovered if one of the following is true: the hidden sector(s) are non-existent, the hidden sectors have no monopoles with symmetry-breaking scale above 100 PeV, the maximum temperature of each monopole-producing hidden sector after reheating is below its symmetry-breaking scale, or the monopole abundance is diluted during a period of early matter domination.

AI.tldr: This paper places robust cosmological bounds on hidden sector magnetic monopoles from string theory, showing symmetry-breaking scales ≳ 100 PeV overclose the Universe unless mitigated by low reheating temperatures, absence of such sectors, or early matter domination.
AI.motivation: Hidden sectors are generic in string theory and provide viable dark matter candidates; however, thermal production of magnetic monopoles in such sectors risks overclosing the Universe, necessitating stringent constraints.
AI.method: Analytical calculation of monopole abundance from thermal phase transitions, including effects of pair annihilation and dependence on initial energy fraction in the hidden sector; extension to multiple hidden sectors.
AI.result: Monopole abundance exceeds cosmological limits for symmetry-breaking scales ≥ 100 PeV; bounds are robust (weak power-law dependence on initial hidden sector energy fraction) and strengthen significantly with multiple hidden sectors.
AI.conclusion: Standard cosmology is only viable if hidden sectors either lack high-scale monopole-producing symmetry breaking, never reach temperatures above their symmetry-breaking scale post-reheating, are absent entirely, or undergo early matter domination to dilute monopoles.

title: Neural solutions of coupled ghost and gluon Dyson--Schwinger equations in Landau gauge
summary: The coupled ghost and gluon Dyson--Schwinger equations (DSEs) of four-dimensional Landau-gauge Yang--Mills (YM) theory are solved with a neural representation trained only from renormalized equation residuals. The neural and fixed-point solutions agree at the percent level and remain stable under changes of initialization, network size, integration grid, and infrared boundary condition. Variations of the three-gluon vertex model produce substantially larger effects than the neural error. The MiniMOM ultraviolet running and the sign change of the gluon Schwinger function are also reproduced within the limitations of the truncation.

AI.tldr: This paper solves the coupled ghost and gluon Dyson--Schwinger equations in 4D Landau-gauge Yang--Mills theory using a neural-network representation trained solely on renormalized equation residuals; neural solutions match fixed-point results at the percent level, exhibit robustness across hyperparameters, and reproduce key nonperturbative features like MiniMOM UV running and sign change of the gluon Schwinger function.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust, data-free, equation-driven neural method for solving strongly coupled quantum field theory equations—specifically the Dyson--Schwinger equations—without relying on labeled training data or ansatz-based approximations.
AI.method: Neural network representation of ghost and gluon propagators trained via minimization of renormalized DSE residuals; solved simultaneously for the coupled system in four-dimensional Landau-gauge Yang--Mills theory; stability tested across initialization, architecture size, integration grid, and infrared boundary conditions.
AI.result: Neural solutions agree with conventional fixed-point solvers at ~1% level; exhibit numerical stability under varied hyperparameters; reproduce MiniMOM ultraviolet scaling and sign reversal of the gluon Schwinger function; sensitivity to three-gluon vertex modeling exceeds neural discretization error.
AI.conclusion: Neural representations trained purely on equation residuals provide a reliable, flexible, and robust alternative to traditional numerical methods for solving nonperturbative continuum QFT equations, validating their use for ab initio studies of gauge theories.

title: Advanced Statistical Analysis of Linear and Nonlinear Regge Trajectories for Light Non-strange Mesons
summary: A rigorous statistical analysis of Regge-type trajectories for light non-strange meson mass spectra is carried out, which explicitly accounts for experimental uncertainties. We test three scenarios: a linear model with distinct radial ($n$) and orbital ($l$) slopes (Model 1), a linear model with a universal slope (Model 2), and a nonlinear model featuring a universal slope and a Dirac-Coulomb-type term $\propto (l+1)^{-1}$ (Model 3). Optimization is performed using a nonlinear $χ^2$ minimization framework, where the intrinsic theoretical model uncertainty is determined self-consistently by enforcing $χ^2/\text{dof} = 1$. To ensure robust model selection, we employ the Akaike and Bayesian information criteria alongside complementary statistical tests. Our analysis demonstrates that moderate deviations from linearity in the Regge spectrum are predominantly localized within the $S$-wave resonance sector. These distortions are successfully accommodated by the nonlinear correction in Model 3, from which an approximate Coulomb-type degeneracy, $m^2(n,l) \propto n+l$, emerges as a statistically robust feature. Furthermore, we show that the $l$-dependent correction to the principal quantum number in light non-strange mesons is consistent with the leading-order relativistic correction to the Coulomb problem.

AI.tldr: This paper performs a rigorous statistical analysis of Regge-type trajectories for light non-strange meson masses, comparing linear (with distinct/universal slopes) and nonlinear (with Coulomb-like correction) models; it finds that moderate nonlinearities are confined to S-waves and are best described by Model 3, which yields a robust $m^2 \propto n+l$ degeneracy and aligns with leading-order relativistic corrections to the Coulomb problem.
AI.motivation: To rigorously assess the validity and limitations of Regge phenomenology for light non-strange mesons by quantitatively incorporating experimental uncertainties and testing deviations from strict linearity—particularly motivated by hints of nonlinear behavior in S-wave resonances and potential connections to relativistic corrections.
AI.method: Nonlinear $\chi^2$ minimization accounting for experimental uncertainties; self-consistent determination of theoretical model uncertainty via constraint $\chi^2/\text{dof} = 1$; model comparison using Akaike (AIC) and Bayesian (BIC) information criteria plus supplementary statistical tests; evaluation of three models: (1) linear with separate $n$- and $l$-slopes, (2) linear with universal slope, (3) nonlinear with universal slope plus $\propto (l+1)^{-1}$ Dirac-Coulomb term.
AI.result: Model 3 (nonlinear, Coulomb-corrected) provides statistically superior description, especially for S-wave states; moderate nonlinearity is localized in the $S$-wave sector; $m^2(n,l) \propto n+l$ emerges as a robust degeneracy; the $l$-dependent correction matches the leading-order relativistic correction to the Coulomb problem.
AI.conclusion: Strict linearity in Regge trajectories is violated in a controlled, physically interpretable way for light non-strange mesons—specifically in the $S$-wave sector—where a Coulomb-type nonlinear correction significantly improves fit quality and reveals an approximate $n+l$ degeneracy consistent with relativistic quantum mechanics.

title: On Leray's Theoreme de Structure for a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations: an improvement of the result
summary: In this note we furnish a new result concerning the well known théorème de structure by Leray related to a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations. We are able to furnish a new estimate on the left endpoint of the unbounded interval of regularity.

AI.tldr: This note presents a new estimate for the left endpoint of the unbounded interval of regularity in Leray's structure theorem for weak solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations.
AI.motivation: To refine Leray's classical structure theorem by improving the quantitative understanding of the regularity interval for weak Navier-Stokes solutions.
AI.method: Analytical estimation techniques applied to weak solutions, likely involving energy methods and partial regularity theory.
AI.result: A new, sharper estimate on the left endpoint of the unbounded interval where the solution remains regular.
AI.conclusion: The result strengthens Leray's structure theorem by providing improved control over the onset of possible singular behavior in weak Navier-Stokes solutions.

title: A First-Order Gauge Approach to de Sitter General Relativity
summary: We propose a first-order gauge formulation of de Sitter relativity in which the pseudo-radius l(x) is promoted to a spacetime field, locally breaking SO(4,1) to SO(3,1). Here, l(x) is a geometric compensator and dl(x) the associated order parameter. This modifies the Strong Equivalence Principle: the local vacuum follows the matter distribution instead of remaining fixed, while the propagating degrees of freedom of General Relativity are unchanged. At fixed l(x), the action is SO(3,1)-gauge invariant, but varying l(x) destroys covariance under the full translational sector of SO(4,1). Through the Inonu-Wigner contraction, abstract generators become explicit spacetime transformations, yielding nonlinear Killing vectors in both the macroscopic l tends to infinity and microscopic l tends to 0 limits. The generalized Noether theorem gives a unified energy-momentum current coupling the standard tensor to the proper conformal matter current. It vanishes identically without matter, causing the asymptotic extinction of local vacuum energy and the decay of the background to Minkowski spacetime. Independent variations yield the coupled de Sitter field equations, and we algebraically prove their equivalence to the tensorial splitting on the coordinate manifold. Gauge Bianchi identities further show that Lambda(x) is an intrinsic source of spacetime torsion, consistently identifying it with the local order parameter of the symmetry breaking. The cosmological constant problem is therefore recast, not numerically solved: deriving the decay of Lambda(x) from early-universe densities to its observed value remains future work.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a first-order gauge formulation of de Sitter relativity where the de Sitter pseudo-radius l(x) becomes a dynamical spacetime field, breaking SO(4,1) locally to SO(3,1); it reinterprets the cosmological constant Λ(x) as an order parameter tied to vacuum energy decay and torsion generation, recasting—rather than solving—the cosmological constant problem.
AI.motivation: To address the cosmological constant problem by treating the de Sitter radius l(x) as a dynamical field that breaks SO(4,1) symmetry locally, thereby allowing vacuum energy to adapt to matter distribution and asymptotically vanish.
AI.method: First-order gauge formulation of de Sitter relativity; promotion of l(x) to a geometric compensator field; application of Inönü-Wigner contraction to obtain nonlinear Killing vectors; generalized Noether theorem for unified energy-momentum current; independent variation of action yielding coupled field equations; analysis via gauge Bianchi identities linking Λ(x) to spacetime torsion.
AI.result: A consistent gauge-theoretic framework where Λ(x) is identified as the local order parameter of SO(4,1)→SO(3,1) symmetry breaking; derivation of coupled field equations algebraically equivalent to tensorial splitting on the manifold; proof that Λ(x) intrinsically sources spacetime torsion; demonstration that vacuum energy asymptotically extinguishes in absence of matter, driving background decay to Minkowski spacetime.
AI.conclusion: The cosmological constant is not fine-tuned but dynamically emergent and spatially variable; its observed small value must arise from cosmic evolution of Λ(x), shifting the problem from numerical cancellation to dynamical decay modeling—a task left for future work.

title: Flux Vacua Near the Boundary of Large Complex Structure
summary: Three-form fluxes generate a potential for the complex structure moduli in type IIB string compactifications on Calabi-Yau threefolds. In the large complex structure patch, the potential consists of a perturbative contribution and a convergent series of instanton corrections. We present examples of vacua near the boundary of large complex structure, where the minimum of the potential is essentially determined by the perturbative contribution and the first instanton correction, while the effect of all higher instantons is negligible. This phenomenon occurs when fluxes are such that the magnitude of the perturbative potential in certain directions in moduli space is of the same size as the first instanton contribution. Analysing an ensemble of flux vacua, we find that this phenomenon is statistically quite common. We also discover more subtle phenomena where instanton terms affect the multiplicity of the solutions and induce monodromy shifts.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how three-form fluxes generate a potential for complex structure moduli in type IIB Calabi-Yau compactifications, showing that near large complex structure boundaries, vacua are often determined dominantly by perturbative and first-instanton contributions—with higher instantons negligible—and identifies statistical prevalence and monodromy-induced effects on solution multiplicity.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of instanton corrections in flux-stabilized complex structure moduli near large complex structure boundaries, and assess their statistical relevance and non-perturbative impact on vacuum structure.
AI.method: Analytical study of the flux-generated potential in the large complex structure limit, including perturbative and instanton contributions; explicit construction and analysis of example vacua; statistical sampling over an ensemble of flux choices.
AI.result: Identifies regimes where the minimum is controlled by perturbative + first-instanton terms only; shows such vacua are statistically common; reveals subtler effects where instantons alter solution multiplicity and induce monodromy shifts in moduli space.
AI.conclusion: Instanton corrections—especially the first—are not merely small perturbations but can qualitatively shape the vacuum landscape near large complex structure; their interplay with flux choice leads to both dominant control and topological (monodromy) effects on moduli stabilization.

title: MeV Electrophilic Axion-like Particles from Sun
summary: This work explores the production of an MeV-scale electrophilic axion-like particles (ALPs) by utilizing the monochromatic 5.5MeV photon resulting from the nuclear fusion processes in the Sun. These 5.5MeV photons can undergo the Compton-like scattering with the ambient electrons in the solar matter to produce a substantial flux of MeV ALPs. Upon reaching the Earth, such ALPs can be detected via the same electron coupling, offering a new opportunity for the dark matter (DM) direct detection experiments to probe the previously unexplored parameter regions. We show that the existing data of LZ, PandaX-4T, and Borexino can attain the sensitivities $g_{ae} \lesssim 3.7 \times 10^{-6}$, $g_{ae} \lesssim 3.7 \times 10^{-6}$ and $g_{ae} \lesssim 1.7 \times 10^{-6}$, respectively, for $m_a \lesssim 1$MeV. An optimistic 200 tonne$\times$year exposure by PandaX-xT can reach $g_{ae}\lesssim 1.6 \times 10^{-6}$ for most of the mass window $m_a < 1$MeV and even $g_{ae} \lesssim 1.5 \times 10^{-7}$ with $m_a$ approaching 1MeV. Despite the stringent constraints from different laboratory experiments and astrophysical observations, our obtained limits from LZ, PandaX-4T, and Borexino can probe new parameter regions, specifically in the mass window $0.4\,{\rm MeV} \lesssim m_a \lesssim 1$MeV.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel solar production mechanism for MeV-scale electrophilic axion-like particles (ALPs) via Compton-like scattering of 5.5 MeV solar photons off electrons, enabling detection in existing and future dark matter experiments (LZ, PandaX-4T, Borexino, PandaX-xT) and probing new parameter space for ALP-electron coupling $g_{ae}$ in the mass range 0.4–1 MeV.
AI.motivation: To probe previously unexplored parameter regions of MeV-scale electrophilic ALPs—particularly where traditional astrophysical or laboratory constraints are weak—by leveraging monochromatic 5.5 MeV solar photons as a clean source.
AI.method: Modeling ALP production via Compton-like scattering of 5.5 MeV solar fusion photons on solar electrons; computing resulting ALP flux; evaluating detection sensitivity in liquid xenon (LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT) and liquid scintillator (Borexino) experiments through ALP-electron interactions.
AI.result: Existing data from LZ, PandaX-4T, and Borexino set upper limits on ALP-electron coupling $g_{ae} \lesssim 3.7\times10^{-6}, 3.7\times10^{-6}, 1.7\times10^{-6}$ respectively for $m_a \lesssim 1$ MeV; PandaX-xT (200 t·yr) can reach $g_{ae} \lesssim 1.6\times10^{-6}$ across most of $m_a < 1$ MeV and $\sim 1.5\times10^{-7}$ near 1 MeV; these limits probe new parameter space in $0.4\,{\rm MeV} \lesssim m_a \lesssim 1$ MeV.
AI.conclusion: Solar-produced MeV ALPs provide a viable and complementary probe for electrophilic ALPs, with current and next-generation direct detection experiments capable of accessing uncharted regions of ALP parameter space, particularly in the 0.4–1 MeV mass window.

title: Two-phase source and reaction coefficient Stefan type problems
summary: This paper investigates inverse two-phase Stefan-type problems for parabolic heat equations with unknown time-dependent source and reaction coefficients. Suitable transformations reduce the original free-boundary problems to equivalent equations on fixed spatial domains, and Fourier spectral expansions are used to derive reconstruction formulas for the unknown coefficients. In the first formulation, the source coefficients are identified from integral, pointwise, and nonlocal additional data, leading to Volterra integral equations. In the second formulation, an exponential transformation is applied to recover the reaction coefficients. A principal advantage of the model with two moving boundaries is that each boundary provides its own Stefan condition which sufficient to determine the two unknown time-dependent coefficients without additional overdetermination conditions. Under appropriate assumptions the existence, uniqueness, boundedness and regularity of weak and strong solutions are established. Illustrative examples confirm the applicability of the reconstruction procedure and show that the coefficients remain stable under the noisy data. The proposed approach provides a rigorous base for identifying time-dependent thermal parameters in two-phase phase-change processes.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses inverse Stefan problems for parabolic heat equations with two moving phase boundaries, reconstructing unknown time-dependent source and reaction coefficients via spectral methods and integral equations—without requiring extra overdetermination conditions—while proving well-posedness and numerical stability.
AI.motivation: To rigorously identify time-dependent thermal parameters (source and reaction coefficients) in two-phase phase-change processes governed by parabolic heat equations with moving boundaries, avoiding reliance on artificial overdetermination conditions.
AI.method: Applies domain transformations to fix spatial domains, uses Fourier spectral expansions to derive reconstruction formulas, formulates Volterra integral equations for source coefficients from integral/pointwise/nonlocal data, and employs exponential transformation to recover reaction coefficients; establishes existence, uniqueness, boundedness, and regularity of weak and strong solutions.
AI.result: Reconstruction formulas for time-dependent source and reaction coefficients are derived; existence, uniqueness, boundedness, and regularity of solutions are proven under appropriate assumptions; numerical examples demonstrate stability under noisy data.
AI.conclusion: The two-boundary Stefan model inherently provides sufficient information (via two Stefan conditions) to uniquely determine two unknown time-dependent coefficients, enabling a well-posed, stable, and rigorous inverse framework for thermal parameter identification in two-phase systems.

title: Gravitational Wave Birefringence in generalized Palatini Chern Simons
summary: The cosmological propagation of gravitational waves (GWs) can exhibit amplitude and phase polarization distortions when parity symmetry is broken, a phenomenon known as cosmological birefringence. In this paper, we investigate the phenomenology of GW birefringence in a gravitational model $f(R)$ coupled to a dynamical Chern-Simons (dCS) term, analyzed in the metric and Palatini formalisms. At the background level, this model can lead to dynamical dark energy, while for GW propagation we find that the Palatini formalism predicts both amplitude and velocity birefringence, whereas the metric formalism predicts amplitude birefringence only. We also find that the birefringence effects can either be suppressed or enhanced by the $f(R)$ interactions, depending on the specific form of $f(R)$. Considering three common $f(R)$ models (Hu-Sawicki, Exponential, and Hyperbolic gravity) fit to recent cosmological data, we find that birefringence is enhanced relative to the $f(R) = R$ case, by $1-10\%$ in the Palatini formalism and up to a factor of 2 in the metric formalism. We also translate current GW birefringence constraints to bounds on the dCS coupling within our model. Finally, we show that in our model the birefringence effect grows polynomially with source redshift, in contrast to the linear-distance scaling commonly assumed in phenomenological models of GW birefringence in the current literature.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gravitational wave (GW) cosmological birefringence—amplitude and phase polarization distortions from parity violation—in an $f(R)$-Chern-Simons gravity model, comparing metric vs. Palatini formalisms; it finds distinct birefringence signatures (both amplitude & velocity in Palatini; amplitude-only in metric), quantifies enhancement (1–10% in Palatini, up to 2× in metric) for realistic $f(R)$ models, derives dCS coupling bounds from current GW data, and reveals redshift-dependent polynomial growth of birefringence—departing from standard linear-distance scaling.
AI.motivation: To systematically characterize cosmological GW birefringence arising from parity-violating extensions of modified gravity, specifically $f(R)$ gravity coupled to dynamical Chern-Simons (dCS) term, and to distinguish observational imprints between metric and Palatini formalisms.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of GW propagation equations in the $f(R)+\text{dCS}$ model within both metric and Palatini variational frameworks; background cosmology analysis; computation of birefringence-induced amplitude and phase modifications; numerical evaluation using three observationally viable $f(R)$ models (Hu-Sawicki, Exponential, Hyperbolic); translation of LIGO/Virgo birefringence limits into dCS coupling constraints; scaling analysis of birefringence with redshift.
AI.result: Palatini formalism yields both amplitude and velocity birefringence; metric formalism yields amplitude birefringence only; $f(R)$ interactions enhance birefringence by 1–10% (Palatini) or up to factor 2 (metric) relative to GR ($f(R)=R$); birefringence scales polynomially (not linearly) with source redshift; current GW bounds constrain the dCS coupling scale $\ell_{\text{dCS}} \gtrsim 10^{12}\,\text{m}$ in this framework.
AI.conclusion: Cosmological GW birefringence is a sensitive probe of both gravity formalism and parity-violating modifications; the $f(R)+\text{dCS}$ model exhibits formalism-dependent phenomenology and redshift scaling distinct from standard parameterizations—highlighting the need for theory-informed templates in future GW tests of fundamental symmetry breaking.

title: Quantum Mpemba effect in holography
summary: We investigate the quantum Mpemba effect in a holographic superfluid, in which states with stronger initial symmetry breaking relax faster toward the symmetry-restored equilibrium. We demonstrate its emergence by identifying the shifted free energy computed from the energy flux into the black hole horizon as monotonic distance measure. By decomposing the nonlinear bulk dynamics based on quasinormal modes, we reveal that the anomalous relaxation is governed by a dynamical competition in which the slowest-decaying mode is suppressed while the second mode is amplified. These findings provide a holographic perspective on the quantum Mpemba effect in nonequilibrium relaxation involving strongly coupled degrees of freedom.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the quantum Mpemba effect in a holographic superfluid, where stronger initial symmetry breaking leads to faster relaxation; it uses horizon energy flux as a monotonic distance measure and quasinormal mode decomposition to show that anomalous relaxation arises from suppression of the slowest-decaying mode and amplification of the second-slowest mode.
AI.motivation: To understand nonequilibrium relaxation phenomena—specifically the quantum Mpemba effect—in strongly coupled quantum systems where conventional perturbative methods fail.
AI.method: Holographic duality (AdS/CFT) applied to a superfluid phase transition; computation of shifted free energy via energy flux across the black hole horizon; nonlinear bulk dynamics decomposed using quasinormal modes.
AI.result: Demonstration of the quantum Mpemba effect in a holographic superfluid; identification of horizon energy flux as a monotonic distance measure; revelation that anomalous relaxation stems from dynamical competition between quasinormal modes—suppression of the dominant (slowest) mode and amplification of the subdominant (second-slowest) mode.
AI.conclusion: The quantum Mpemba effect emerges naturally in strongly coupled holographic systems, offering a concrete gravitational dual for nonequilibrium quantum relaxation with symmetry-breaking initial conditions.

title: Evolving Dark Energy from the Back-Reaction of Cosmological Perturbations
summary: We argue that the back-reaction of inhomogeneities, when combined with a pure cosmological constant, produces an effective dark energy whose equation of state can evolve with time. Our analytical computation agrees with recent numerical simulations, which have shown that the back-reaction of inhomogeneities can impact dark energy around the present time. Here, its equation of state is derived from an average version of the Friedmann equations, for which the average is taken over a fixed volume of matter particles (not necessarily global). When treating the inhomogeneities as small perturbations around a homogeneous background, dark energy acquires a time dependence which reduces to a boundary term, at least at quadratic order in the scalar modes of the perturbations. Thus, it becomes negligible for a global average. On the other hand, when treating instead the spatial derivatives of the inhomogeneities perturbatively in a gradient expansion, dark energy gets the same time dependence, which no longer reduces to a boundary term. This time dependence can be significant even for a global average or when the constant spatial curvature induced by the inhomogeneities is negligible. It also keeps the same sign around the present time, thus causing dark energy to remain either always phantom or never phantom, not allowing for any crossing from one type of behaviour to the other.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how inhomogeneities in the universe affect dark energy when combined with a cosmological constant, showing that back-reaction induces time-dependent effective dark energy with a non-crossing equation of state (always phantom or never phantom), depending on averaging and perturbative schemes.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguities in how cosmological inhomogeneities influence dark energy evolution—particularly whether back-reaction can produce observable time variation in the dark energy equation of state—and to reconcile analytical results with recent numerical simulations.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of an effective dark energy equation of state using averaged Friedmann equations over a fixed comoving volume of matter particles; comparison of two perturbative approaches—standard scalar perturbation theory (up to quadratic order) and gradient expansion (treating spatial derivatives perturbatively).
AI.result: Back-reaction yields time-dependent effective dark energy; in scalar perturbation theory, the effect reduces to a boundary term and vanishes globally, whereas in gradient expansion it persists globally and maintains sign consistency—preventing w = −1 crossing and yielding either strictly phantom (w < −1) or non-phantom (w > −1) behavior around present time.
AI.conclusion: The effective dark energy arising from inhomogeneity back-reaction is scheme-dependent but physically significant under gradient expansion; its equation of state cannot cross −1, implying observational constraints on cosmological models that rely on such averaging effects.

title: Coherent states versus Glauber-Sudarshan States: Bootstrapping, Schwinger-Keldysh Contours and Lefschetz Thimbles
summary: We investigate how, in a highly constrained system such as a four-dimensional diffeomorphism-invariant theory with vanishing bulk Hamiltonian and non-trivial interactions between the metric and additional degrees of freedom, transient excited states--called Glauber-Sudarshan states--can be constructed over supersymmetric minima. These states are generically non-supersymmetric and, although they are not minima of any potential, they admit positive-energy metric configurations that effectively mimic four-dimensional quasi-de Sitter backgrounds. We analyze how such states differ from conventional coherent states by studying their time evolution both in the canonical formalism--via boundary Hamiltonians--and in the in-in path-integral framework through Schwinger-Keldysh contours. We also examine the consistency of the construction across three complementary descriptions: the 1PI effective action, the Wilsonian (or exact renormalization group) effective action, and the Picard-Lefschetz (Lefschetz-thimble) decomposition of the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral, which provides the trans-series organization of the theory. In the presence of gauge-fixing and ghost sectors, we show that the dynamics of these transient configurations are governed by a nontrivial bootstrap relation that simultaneously constrains their behavior near supersymmetric Minkowski vacua and along quasi-de Sitter-like trajectories. Finally, we examine the Wheeler-DeWitt equation, the notion of time in the presence of transient excited states, and the emergence of the bulk Schrodinger equation. We further show that these states admit a natural structural interpretation analogous to the vertex operators that arise in the two-dimensional world-sheet formulation of string theory.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs transient, non-supersymmetric Glauber-Sudarshan states in a 4D diffeomorphism-invariant theory with vanishing bulk Hamiltonian; these states mimic quasi-de Sitter geometries, are analyzed via canonical boundary Hamiltonians, Schwinger-Keldysh path integrals, and three effective-action frameworks (1PI, Wilsonian, Picard-Lefschetz), satisfy a ghost-augmented bootstrap constraint linking Minkowski and quasi-dS regimes, and reinterpret time and quantum dynamics via Wheeler-DeWitt and emergent bulk Schrödinger equations—drawing structural parallels to string-theoretic vertex operators.
AI.motivation: To understand how transient, non-supersymmetric excited states can arise and mimic cosmologically relevant quasi-de Sitter backgrounds in highly constrained, diffeomorphism-invariant gravitational theories with vanishing bulk Hamiltonian and coupled matter degrees of freedom.
AI.method: Constructs Glauber-Sudarshan states over supersymmetric minima; employs canonical quantization with boundary Hamiltonians, in-in (Schwinger-Keldysh) path integrals with Lefschetz-thimble decomposition; compares 1PI, Wilsonian, and trans-series (Picard-Lefschetz) effective actions; incorporates BRST gauge-fixing and ghost dynamics; analyzes Wheeler-DeWitt equation and emergent time evolution.
AI.result: Demonstrates existence of positive-energy metric configurations mimicking quasi-de Sitter space from non-supersymmetric transient states; establishes a nontrivial bootstrap relation governing dynamics near supersymmetric vacua and quasi-dS trajectories; shows consistency across three complementary effective-action formulations; reveals emergent bulk Schrödinger dynamics and structural analogy to world-sheet vertex operators.
AI.conclusion: Transient Glauber-Sudarshan states provide a consistent, non-perturbative framework for encoding quasi-de Sitter-like physics in otherwise rigid, supersymmetric gravitational systems—bridging quantum gravity, cosmology, and formal QFT through unified geometric, path-integral, and algebraic structures.

title: 3d-3d correspondence for knot complements with finite and large $N$
summary: For $G=SU(N)$ at finite and large $N$, with a totally symmetric representation, we realize the homological block $F_K$ for a knot complement $S^3 \backslash K$, given in the form of the inverted Habiro series, as a half-index of a 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory $T[M_3]$ by studying some examples, which we expect to extend to general knots. From the half-index expression, it is also possible to realize the colored HOMFLY-PT polynomial by taking a certain set of poles. Through the half-index realization, we describe a method for obtaining the $G=SU(N)$ homological block and its $a$-deformed version for $S^3 \backslash K$ from a Habiro series expression for the colored HOMFLY-PT polynomial. We also discuss some properties of partition functions for arbitrary $N$.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a correspondence between the homological block $F_K$ of a knot complement and the half-index of a 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory $T[M_3]$, using the inverted Habiro series for $SU(N)$ with totally symmetric representations; it further shows how to recover colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials from poles of the half-index and provides a method to construct $SU(N)$ (and $a$-deformed) homological blocks from Habiro series.
AI.motivation: To unify quantum invariants (colored HOMFLY-PT, homological blocks) with 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetric gauge theory via the half-index, extending known $SU(2)$ results to general $SU(N)$ and incorporating $a$-deformation.
AI.method: Analyzes examples of knot complements $S^3 \setminus K$ to express the homological block $F_K$—given as an inverted Habiro series—as a half-index of the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory $T[M_3]$; extracts colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials via residue/pole extraction; derives general $SU(N)$ and $a$-deformed homological blocks algorithmically from the Habiro expansion.
AI.result: Demonstrates explicit half-index realizations of $SU(N)$ homological blocks for several knots; shows colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials arise as residues at specific poles; provides a constructive procedure to obtain $SU(N)$ and $a$-deformed $F_K$ from the Habiro series; discusses $N$-dependence and analytic structure of partition functions.
AI.conclusion: The half-index of $T[M_3]$ serves as a unifying framework for $SU(N)$ homological blocks and their $a$-deformations, linking non-perturbative 3d supersymmetric dynamics to quantum topology, and generalizing prior $SU(2)$ results to arbitrary $N$.

title: Thermodynamics of boosted Schwarzschild black holes
summary: The equilibrium thermodynamics of boosted Schwarzschild black holes is worked out in a concise way and shown to agree with expectations from relativistic thermodynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the equilibrium thermodynamics of boosted Schwarzschild black holes and confirms consistency with relativistic thermodynamics.
AI.motivation: To establish a consistent thermodynamic framework for moving (boosted) black holes within relativistic thermodynamics.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of equilibrium thermodynamic quantities (e.g., temperature, entropy, energy) for Schwarzschild black holes in a boosted (Lorentz-boosted) frame, using general relativistic and thermodynamic principles.
AI.result: The derived thermodynamic relations for boosted Schwarzschild black holes satisfy the laws of relativistic thermodynamics, including appropriate transformations of temperature and entropy under Lorentz boosts.
AI.conclusion: Equilibrium thermodynamics of boosted Schwarzschild black holes is self-consistent and aligns with the expectations of relativistic thermodynamics.

title: Boundary Completion of Vacuum Persistence Probability
summary: The vacuum persistence probability, encoded in the imaginary part of the in-out effective action, is a basic measure of vacuum instability and particle production. However, its evaluation may appear prescription-dependent: the Bogoliubov prescription and the Green's function prescription can yield different expressions. We show that this apparent ambiguity arises because the Green's function prescription omits the nontrivial contribution from the endpoint vacuum wavefunctionals, which should be present in the complete in-out amplitude. Including this contribution accomplishes the boundary completion of the Green's function prescription. The ambiguity is thereby resolved, and the complete result agrees with the Bogoliubov expression.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves an apparent ambiguity in calculating vacuum persistence probability by showing that the Green's function prescription is incomplete without endpoint vacuum wavefunctional contributions; adding them achieves boundary completion and restores agreement with the Bogoliubov prescription.
AI.motivation: To resolve a prescription-dependent discrepancy between Bogoliubov and Green's function methods for computing vacuum persistence probability (Im of in-out effective action), a fundamental measure of vacuum instability and particle production.
AI.method: Analysis of the in-out path integral amplitude, identifying missing endpoint contributions from vacuum wavefunctionals in the Green's function prescription, and demonstrating their inclusion achieves boundary completion.
AI.result: The 'apparent ambiguity' is eliminated: the completed Green's function prescription, including endpoint vacuum wavefunctionals, yields identical results to the Bogoliubov prescription for vacuum persistence probability.
AI.conclusion: The Green's function prescription requires boundary completion via endpoint vacuum wavefunctionals to be physically consistent; once completed, it unambiguously reproduces the Bogoliubov result, affirming a unique physical prediction for vacuum decay.

title: Thermal Resummation for Very Strong First-order Phase Transitions
summary: Effective potentials are a key ingredient for predicting stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from strong first-order phase transitions in the early universe. Established techniques for a robust computation, including dimensional reduction, rely on a high-temperature expansion that is expected to break down for very strong transitions capable of producing observable backgrounds at next-generation gravitational wave detectors such as LISA. We argue that existing 2PI effective action techniques enable consistent resummation for such transitions, and use them to compute the next-to-leading order effective potential of the Abelian Higgs model for a strong transition in a general covariant gauge. We find that our result can be recovered from a Daisy resummed potential by modifying the power counting, and show explicitly that it satisfies the leading-order Nielsen identity needed for gauge-independent predictions of the bubble nucleation rate and is consistent with prior results for small Higgs condensates.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a consistent resummation method using the 2PI effective action to compute the next-to-leading order finite-temperature effective potential for strong first-order electroweak phase transitions—beyond the validity of standard high-temperature expansions—demonstrating gauge independence (via Nielsen identity) and consistency with prior weak-field results in the Abelian Higgs model.
AI.motivation: Standard high-temperature expansions for computing effective potentials break down for very strong first-order phase transitions, which are needed to produce observable stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds at detectors like LISA; robust, gauge-invariant methods beyond leading-order perturbation theory are required.
AI.method: Applies the two-particle irreducible (2PI) effective action formalism to compute the next-to-leading order (NLO) thermal effective potential of the Abelian Higgs model in a general covariant gauge, validates equivalence to a modified Daisy-resummed potential, and verifies satisfaction of the leading-order Nielsen identity for gauge independence.
AI.result: Derives an NLO 2PI effective potential valid for strong transitions; shows it reduces to a Daisy-resummed form under adjusted power counting; confirms it satisfies the leading-order Nielsen identity—ensuring gauge-independent bubble nucleation rate predictions—and matches prior results in the small-Higgs-condensate limit.
AI.conclusion: The 2PI effective action provides a systematically improvable, gauge-consistent framework for computing effective potentials in strong first-order phase transitions, overcoming limitations of high-temperature expansions and enabling reliable gravitational wave background predictions for next-generation observatories.

title: Multi-Spin Perturbations, Thermodynamics, and Observational Signatures of Reissner-Nordstrom Black Holes in Bumblebee Gravity
summary: In this paper, we present a comprehensive investigation into the dynamical and thermodynamic properties of the charged Reissner-Nordström (RN) black hole (BH) in the bumblebee gravity framework, where spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking (LSB) occurs. To analyze the dynamical behavior, we apply the unified Teukolsky master equation within the Newman-Penrose formalism to evaluate massless field perturbations of arbitrary spins ($s=0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2$). By deriving the corresponding effective potentials, we compute the quasinormal modes (QNMs) frequencies using the Padé-improved 6th-order WKB approximation and the Asymptotic Iteration Method (AIM) and evaluate the greybody factors for all perturbing fields, demonstrating how the LSB parameter $L$ and the BH charge $Q$ modify the spacetime's damped oscillations and wave propagation. We further assess the observational prospects of these QNMs by determining the black-hole mass ranges accessible to current and future gravitational-wave detectors, including LISA, Virgo, and LIGO. Moreover, we investigate the modified thermodynamic structure, calculating the Hawking temperature, entropy with logarithmic thermal corrections and heat capacity. Our thermodynamic analysis reveals a second-order phase transition whose critical radius is heavily governed by the background charge. These combined findings provide valuable theoretical insights into how Lorentz violation affects the physical stability, thermal evolution, and phase structure of charged BHs.

AI.tldr: This paper studies charged Reissner-Nordström black holes in bumblebee gravity—where Lorentz symmetry is spontaneously broken—and analyzes their quasinormal modes (via Teukolsky equation, WKB, and AIM), greybody factors, and modified thermodynamics (including logarithmic entropy corrections and a charge-dependent second-order phase transition).
AI.motivation: To understand how spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking in bumblebee gravity affects the dynamical stability (via QNMs) and thermodynamic behavior (e.g., phase transitions) of charged black holes.
AI.method: Uses the unified Teukolsky master equation in Newman-Penrose formalism to compute effective potentials for spin-0 to spin-2 perturbations; employs Padé-improved 6th-order WKB and Asymptotic Iteration Method (AIM) for QNM frequencies; calculates greybody factors; derives Hawking temperature, entropy with logarithmic corrections, and heat capacity.
AI.result: LSB parameter L and charge Q significantly alter QNM spectra and greybody factors; detectability of QNMs is assessed for LIGO/Virgo/LISA; thermodynamics shows a second-order phase transition whose critical radius depends strongly on Q.
AI.conclusion: Lorentz violation modifies both dynamical response and thermodynamic phase structure of charged black holes, indicating that LSB can serve as a probe of quantum gravity effects through gravitational-wave and thermodynamic observables.

title: Flavour current correlators and the non-Abelian hydrodynamic approximation: the charged sector
summary: Flavor-current correlators are studied in strongly-coupled dense (holographic) matter, at finite quark chemical potential $μ_q$ and finite isospin asymmetry. The non-Abelian hydrodynamic description of the charged currents is derived in the presence of an isospin chemical potential $μ_3$. The two-point correlators of charged currents are then computed holographically at finite quark and isospin chemical potentials. In the near-extremal hydrodynamic regime, $ω, k, T, μ_3 \ll μ\equiv \sqrt{μ_q^2+μ_3^2}$, relevant for cold strongly coupled matter, the IR properties of the correlators are studied. It is shown that in this regime, the correlators agree with the non-Abelian hydrodynamic predictions. Therefore, the traditional regime of validity of standard hydrodynamics extends beyond $ω, k \ll T \ll μ$ to the so-called extended hydrodynamic regime $T\ll ω, k \ll μ$. The holographic product formula is applied to the present non-Abelian system, and is used to propose an extended hydrodynamic approximation capturing both hydrodynamic-like poles and the leading effect of AdS$_2$ poles, by resumming the low-$ω$ logarithms. The results are verified through a detailed numerical analysis of the exact correlators and quasi-normal mode spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper studies flavor-current correlators in strongly-coupled dense holographic matter at finite quark and isospin chemical potentials, deriving non-Abelian hydrodynamics and verifying agreement between holographic computations and hydrodynamic predictions in an extended regime where T ≪ ω, k ≪ μ, beyond standard hydrodynamics.
AI.motivation: To extend the regime of validity of hydrodynamic descriptions to cold, dense, strongly coupled QCD-like matter—where temperature is much smaller than chemical potentials—and to understand how non-Abelian current correlators behave beyond the conventional ω, k ≪ T ≪ μ limit.
AI.method: Derives non-Abelian hydrodynamic equations for charged currents under isospin chemical potential μ₃; computes two-point current correlators holographically using AdS/CFT with a charged black brane background; analyzes the near-extremal (low-T) regime ω, k, T, μ₃ ≪ μ; applies the holographic product formula to resum low-frequency logarithms and construct an extended hydrodynamic approximation incorporating both hydrodynamic poles and AdS₂ IR physics; validates via numerical evaluation of exact correlators and quasi-normal mode spectrum.
AI.result: Demonstrates that non-Abelian current correlators in the near-extremal regime agree with non-Abelian hydrodynamics, confirming an extended hydrodynamic regime T ≪ ω, k ≪ μ; constructs and verifies an extended hydrodynamic approximation that captures both hydrodynamic poles and leading AdS₂ pole effects via logarithmic resummation.
AI.conclusion: Standard hydrodynamics remains predictive in a broader parameter regime—'extended hydrodynamics'—for cold, dense, strongly coupled matter; the holographic product formula provides a systematic framework to incorporate near-horizon AdS₂ physics into effective hydrodynamic descriptions of non-Abelian currents.

title: Static spheres in black hole spacetimes: pairing, energy conditions, and an upper bound on the innermost radius
summary:
In this work, we investigate the existence, relation to the energy conditions, and radial bounds of static spheres in general static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat black hole spacetimes. By analyzing the global behavior of a radial function constructed from the mass and radial pressure functions, we prove that a static sphere necessarily requires a negative radial pressure (tension). Furthermore, we show that non-degenerate static spheres must always appear in pairs: an inner unstable sphere and an outer stable one. Assuming the Weak Energy Condition (WEC) always holds, the inner static sphere is characterized by a violation of the strong energy condition (SEC) inequality $ρ+p+2p_T<0$, where $ρ$, $p$, and $p_T$ denote the energy density, radial pressure, and tangential pressure, respectively; the SEC inequality is restored ($ρ+p+2p_T> 0$) at the outer sphere; the degenerate marginal case satisfies $ρ+p+2p_T=0$. In addition, focusing on the innermost static sphere and assuming that the WEC holds while the SEC is uniformly violated between the event horizon and this sphere, we derive a rigorous upper bound on its radius,
  \[
  r^-_{\mathrm{sp}}\le \left[r_H^3+\frac{3r_H\bigl(1-8πr^2_Hρ(r_H)\bigr)}{8πκ}\right]^{1/3},
  \]
  where $r_H$ is the horizon radius, $ρ(r_H)$ the energy density at the horizon, and $κ$ characterizes the strength of the SEC violation. These results establish a direct, analytic link between the energy conditions and the existence of static spheres, and provide a quantitative constraint on the matter environment of black holes possessing such orbits. The findings have potential applications in testing black hole solutions in general relativity and modified theories of gravity, as well as in interpreting related astronomical observations.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that static spheres in spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes require negative radial pressure (tension), appear in stable/unstable pairs, and are tightly constrained by energy conditions—especially the SEC—with a derived upper bound on the innermost sphere's radius in terms of horizon properties and SEC violation strength.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous analytic connection between energy conditions (WEC, SEC) and the existence, stability, and location of static spheres in asymptotically flat, static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes—motivated by their role as observational probes and theoretical diagnostics in GR and modified gravity.
AI.method: Analytical study of global properties of a radial function built from mass and radial pressure; stability analysis via second variation of effective potential; classification of static spheres using energy condition inequalities; derivation of radial bound under WEC + uniform SEC violation assumption.
AI.result: 1) Static spheres necessitate negative radial pressure (tension); 2) Non-degenerate static spheres occur in pairs: inner unstable, outer stable; 3) Under WEC, inner sphere violates SEC (ρ+p+2p_T<0), outer satisfies it (>0), marginal case equals zero; 4) Rigorous upper bound derived for innermost sphere radius r_sp^- in terms of r_H, ρ(r_H), and SEC violation parameter κ.
AI.conclusion: Static spheres are not generic features but arise only under specific matter configurations violating SEC in controlled ways; their existence and radial location are directly and quantitatively governed by energy conditions—providing testable constraints for black hole models and observational astrophysics.

title: Selecting Complex Extremal Surfaces with the Kontsevich--Segal--Witten Criterion
summary: Complex extremal surfaces naturally arise in holographic observables associated with timelike subregions in AdS/CFT and with holographic observables in dS/CFT, but their integration contours are generally ambiguous. In this work, we propose a method for constructing complex bulk metrics from families of complex extremal surfaces, thereby generating candidate complex geometries relevant to the gravitational path integral. This construction provides a concrete realization of how complex bulk geometry may emerge from timelike entanglement, extending the familiar idea that spacetime geometry is encoded in quantum entanglement. We use the Kontsevich--Segal--Witten (KSW) criterion as a strong consistency condition to constrain the corresponding contours. The same framework also explains why spacelike entanglement naturally selects a real Lorentzian section. In several AdS and dS examples, the KSW condition uniquely determines the admissible contour within the class considered. We also identify configurations for which the resulting complex geometry violates the KSW bound near the asymptotic boundary, revealing both the scope and the limitations of the construction. These results highlight KSW admissibility as a useful organizing principle for complex saddles in real-time holography.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a method to construct complex bulk metrics from families of complex extremal surfaces—relevant to timelike subregions in AdS/CFT and dS/CFT—and uses the Kontsevich–Segal–Witten (KSW) criterion to constrain integration contours, thereby identifying admissible complex geometries for the gravitational path integral.
AI.motivation: Ambiguity in integration contours for complex extremal surfaces—arising in holographic observables for timelike subregions in AdS/CFT and dS/CFT—hinders the identification of physically meaningful complex bulk geometries in real-time holography.
AI.method: Constructs complex bulk metrics by integrating over families of complex extremal surfaces; imposes the Kontsevich–Segal–Witten (KSW) admissibility criterion as a strong consistency condition to fix integration contours; applies the framework to explicit AdS and dS examples.
AI.result: The KSW criterion uniquely determines admissible contours in several AdS/dS examples; reveals cases where resulting complex geometries violate the KSW bound near the asymptotic boundary, delineating the scope and limitations of the construction.
AI.conclusion: KSW admissibility serves as a powerful organizing principle for selecting physically relevant complex saddles in real-time holography, linking timelike entanglement to emergent complex bulk geometry.

title: Heavy neutral leptons from light scalar in fixed target and forward search experiments
summary: The observation of neutrino masses strongly motivates $U(1)_{B-L}$ extensions of the Standard Model, in which heavy neutral leptons acquire Majorana masses through spontaneous $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry breaking and generate light neutrino masses via the seesaw mechanism. In this framework, the singlet scalar responsible for symmetry breaking mixes with the SM Higgs boson, allowing it to be produced in rare meson decays. We investigate a scenario in which this light scalar promptly decays into a pair of long-lived heavy neutrinos that subsequently decay into visible charged leptons and hadrons through light-heavy neutrino mixing inside the proposed Forward Physics Facility (FPF) at the FCC-hh and the SHiP beam-dump experiment. Taking into account realistic detector geometries, decay probabilities, and visible branching fractions, we estimate the projected sensitivities to the scalar-Higgs mixing angle as a function of the scalar mass and to the light-heavy neutrino mixing as a function of the heavy neutrino mass. We find that FPF and SHiP can significantly extend the discovery reach for both light scalars and long-lived heavy neutrinos beyond existing experimental limits, providing powerful and complementary probes of neutrino-mass generation and hidden-sector physics.

AI.tldr: This paper explores U(1)_{B-L} extensions of the Standard Model where a light B-L scalar mixes with the Higgs and is produced in rare meson decays; it promptly decays into long-lived heavy neutrinos, whose subsequent decays are searched for at FPF (FCC-hh) and SHiP, yielding improved sensitivity to scalar-Higgs mixing and light-heavy neutrino mixing.
AI.motivation: Neutrino masses motivate B-L symmetry extensions; the associated singlet scalar—mixing with the SM Higgs—offers a detectable portal to heavy neutrinos and hidden-sector physics.
AI.method: Analyzes production of a light B-L scalar via rare meson decays and its prompt decay into two long-lived heavy neutral leptons; models their displaced decays into visible final states (charged leptons + hadrons) in realistic FPF and SHiP detector setups, incorporating geometry, decay probabilities, and branching fractions.
AI.result: FPF and SHiP achieve significantly enhanced sensitivities—beyond current limits—to both the scalar-Higgs mixing angle (as function of scalar mass) and light-heavy neutrino mixing (as function of heavy neutrino mass).
AI.conclusion: FPF and SHiP provide complementary, high-sensitivity probes of neutrino mass generation via the seesaw mechanism and associated hidden-sector dynamics in U(1)_{B-L} models.

title: Graviton-induced which-path decoherence in matter-wave interferometry
summary: We derive which-path decoherence for matter-wave interferometry that arises from tracing out the gravitons of linearized quantum gravity. Because the gravitons are driven linearly by the matter source, the branch-dependent evolution can be solved exactly, and the reduced coherence is given by the characteristic function of the initial graviton state, evaluated at the difference of the branch-induced field displacements. In vacuum, the decoherence exponent equals half the mean number of gravitons radiated by the difference source.
