For a smooth Gaussian trajectory, it reduces to $Γ_{\rm vac}=(8/15)\,Gm^2d^4/(\hbar c^5τ^4)$, ranging from $10^{-89}$ to $10^{-61}$ across representative matter-wave platforms. For a general squeezed graviton vacuum, we obtain an exact expression in which squeezing either suppresses or enhances the vacuum response, depending on the squeezing phase. For the strongly squeezed state produced by inflation, this expression reduces to $Γ_{\rm inf}=(π/20)\,Ω_{\rm inf}(md^2H_0/\hbar)^2$ and reaches at most $\sim10^{-27}$ for optimistic parameters. Hence, the which-path decoherence induced by radiative gravitons is therefore negligible in current matter-wave interferometers.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates the decoherence effect on matter-wave interferometers due to graviton emission in linearized quantum gravity, showing it is negligible (e.g., Γ ~ 10⁻⁸⁹–10⁻²⁷) across current experimental platforms.
AI.motivation: To quantify whether radiative gravitons—predicted by linearized quantum gravity—induce measurable which-path decoherence in matter-wave interferometry, a potential test of quantum aspects of gravity.
AI.method: Exact solution of branch-dependent graviton dynamics driven by classical matter sources; computation of reduced coherence via characteristic function of initial graviton state; evaluation for vacuum, squeezed vacuum, and inflationary graviton states.
AI.result: Decoherence exponent Γ_vac = (8/15) G m² d⁴ / (ℏ c⁵ τ⁴) for Gaussian trajectories (~10⁻⁸⁹–10⁻⁶¹); Γ_inf ≈ (π/20) Ω_inf (m d² H₀ / ℏ)² ≤ ~10⁻²⁷ for inflationary squeezing; squeezing phase determines suppression or enhancement.
AI.conclusion: Graviton-induced which-path decoherence is many orders of magnitude too small to be observed in present or near-future matter-wave interferometers.

title: Gauge-Theoretical Method in Solving Zero-curvature Equations III --Gauge Theoretical Method and the Bäcklund Transformations for Solitons--
summary: In soliton theory, both the gauge-theoretical method and the Bäcklund transformation yield soliton equations from the compatibility condition of a pair of linear equations. Therefore, it is necessary to clarify the similarities and differences between these two methods. The Bäcklund transformation defines a transformation from one soliton solution to another. In particular, restricting the transformation to solutions with different soliton numbers yields interesting insights. Using several examples, we demonstrate how soliton solutions with different soliton numbers are constructed.

AI.tldr: This paper compares the gauge-theoretical method and Bäcklund transformation in soliton theory, focusing on how both derive soliton equations from linear compatibility conditions and how Bäcklund transformations generate solutions with varying soliton numbers.
AI.motivation: To clarify the similarities and differences between the gauge-theoretical method and Bäcklund transformation in deriving soliton equations via compatibility conditions of linear systems.
AI.method: Analytical comparison of the two methods; explicit construction of soliton solutions with different soliton numbers using Bäcklund transformations; illustration through representative examples.
AI.result: Demonstrates that Bäcklund transformations can map solutions with distinct soliton numbers, revealing structural relationships among soliton families; highlights conceptual and technical distinctions between gauge-theoretic and Bäcklund approaches.
AI.conclusion: Both methods rely on linear system compatibility but differ in scope and implementation; Bäcklund transformation serves as a powerful tool for generating hierarchies of soliton solutions across different topological sectors (soliton numbers).

title: Using horizon shadows to distinguish a black hole and a white hole
comment: 11 pages, 14 figures. Extended work of Chinese Physics C,49(2):025109 (2025)
summary: Within theoretical frameworks such as loop quantum gravity, black holes may evolve into white holes through a quantum bounce. This paper uses general relativistic ray-tracing techniques to calculate the ray-traced imaging of accretion disks from the previous cosmic stage during the Kerr black hole and post-bounce Kerr white hole phases. Calculations show that the black hole image presents a crescent emission ring and a central shadow. In contrast, after radiation from the previous universe penetrates the rotating white hole, eccentric and asymmetric nested intensity ring structures form in the synthetic image due to frame-dragging and lensing effects. We analyze the influence of spin parameters, observation inclinations, and accretion disk geometric configurations on the distribution of this nested ring structure using synthetic images and intensity profiles. Building upon this, we introduce polarized ray-tracing calculations for radiation across evolutionary stages. This process results in the polarization image features after the polarization vector is subjected to the gravitational field and spacetime spin dragging during the photon propagation through the white hole horizon and internal spacetime. The spatial rotation patterns and concentric interference fringes in the white hole polarization images exhibit a distinct inter-ring polarization discontinuity. This phenomenon differs from the polarization behavior of black holes. The intensity ring structures and polarization inter-ring discontinuity features provide multi-band and polarimetric interferometry baselines to overcome morphological observational degeneracies. This provides theoretical guidance for future very-long-baseline interferometry (VLBI) to distinguish black holes and white holes.

AI.tldr: This paper uses general relativistic ray-tracing to simulate and compare imaging and polarimetric signatures of Kerr black holes and post-bounce Kerr white holes, revealing distinct nested intensity rings and inter-ring polarization discontinuities in white hole images—features that break morphological degeneracies and enable VLBI-based discrimination.
AI.motivation: To distinguish astrophysical black holes from hypothetical white holes resulting from quantum bounces (e.g., in loop quantum gravity), by identifying unique observational signatures in intensity and polarization structure.
AI.method: General relativistic ray-tracing of accretion disk emission across Kerr black hole and post-bounce Kerr white hole spacetimes; includes unpolarized and polarized radiative transfer, incorporating frame-dragging, gravitational lensing, horizon crossing, and spin-induced polarization vector evolution.
AI.result: White hole images exhibit eccentric, asymmetric nested intensity rings (absent in black hole crescent+shadow morphology); polarized images show spatially rotating patterns and concentric interference fringes with sharp inter-ring polarization discontinuities—unlike smooth black hole polarization fields.
AI.conclusion: The combination of nested intensity ring morphology and inter-ring polarization discontinuity provides robust, multi-messenger (intensity + polarization) discriminators for VLBI observations, offering a theoretically grounded pathway to test quantum-gravity-inspired black-to-white-hole transition scenarios.

title: One-point holographic correlator in the expanding universe
comment: 34 Pages Latex, 8 Figures, Comments are welcome
summary: In this article, we have calculated the time-dependent thermal one-point function of massive operators within an expanding universe. We employ the Randall-Sundrum II braneworld model combined with a $p$-brane gas in the bulk, enabling us to represent various matter-dominated cosmological scenarios localised on the brane. Applying the geodesic formula introduced by Grinberg and Maldacena in \cite{Grinberg:2020fdj}, we have calculated the thermal one-point functions of massive operators within the universe. The time-dependent one-point functions for different matter-dominated universes, both single-component and multi-component, are derived from the brane's evolving radial position. The time-dependent positions of the branes have been obtained using the second Israel junction condition. Additionally, we have analyzed the early and late-time behaviors of the thermal one-point function across various matter-dominated universes.

AI.tldr: This paper computes time-dependent thermal one-point functions of massive operators in an expanding universe using the Randall-Sundrum II braneworld model with a p-brane gas in the bulk, leveraging the Grinberg–Maldacena geodesic formula and Israel junction conditions to derive results for single- and multi-component matter-dominated cosmologies.
AI.motivation: To study thermal quantum field theory observables—specifically time-dependent thermal one-point functions—in realistic cosmological settings modeled by braneworld scenarios, bridging holographic thermal physics and early-universe cosmology.
AI.method: Uses the Randall-Sundrum II braneworld setup augmented with a p-brane gas in the bulk; applies the Grinberg–Maldacena geodesic prescription for thermal correlators; determines brane radial evolution via the second Israel junction condition; derives time-dependent one-point functions for massive operators across various matter-dominated eras.
AI.result: Analytic expressions for time-dependent thermal one-point functions of massive operators in single- and multi-component matter-dominated universes; asymptotic analysis revealing distinct early- and late-time scaling behaviors depending on the equation-of-state parameter(s).
AI.conclusion: Thermal one-point functions in braneworld cosmologies exhibit nontrivial time dependence governed by brane dynamics and bulk geometry; the approach provides a concrete holographic framework for probing thermal QFT in time-varying gravitational backgrounds.

title: Gauge coupling beta functions and gauge field anomalous dimensions at four loops in the Standard Model
summary: We present the beta functions of the gauge couplings and the anomalous dimensions of the gauge fields in the unbroken phase of the Standard Model at four loops.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the four-loop beta functions for gauge couplings and anomalous dimensions of gauge fields in the unbroken Standard Model phase.
AI.motivation: To advance precision calculations in quantum field theory and improve the theoretical consistency and predictive power of the Standard Model at high energy scales.
AI.method: Perturbative quantum field theory techniques, specifically multi-loop Feynman diagram computations in dimensional regularization, applied to the unbroken (symmetric) phase of the Standard Model.
AI.result: Complete four-loop expressions for the beta functions of the three SM gauge couplings (SU(3)_C, SU(2)_L, U(1)_Y) and the anomalous dimensions of the corresponding gauge fields.
AI.conclusion: The results provide essential input for high-precision renormalization group evolution, stability analyses of the SM vacuum, and studies of grand unification scenarios.

title: New generalization of the Barboza-Alcaniz parametrization of Dark energy
summary: A generalization of the Barboza-Alcaniz parametrization of dark energy is proposed. This is a three-parameter model which can resolve the shortcomings of the Barboza-Alcaniz behavior at future times. We show that cosmological data favor the new parametrization over both the Barboza-Alcaniz model and $Λ$CDM. We also consider the cosmological implications of the model and show that the qualitative behavior mimics to the original Barboza-Alcaniz model, with a slightly smaller acceleration rate.

AI.tldr: Proposes a three-parameter generalization of the Barboza-Alcaniz dark energy parametrization that improves future-time behavior and is statistically favored over both the original Barboza-Alcaniz model and ΛCDM.
AI.motivation: To resolve the shortcomings of the Barboza-Alcaniz parametrization at late (future) cosmic times while retaining its descriptive power for dark energy evolution.
AI.method: Introduces a generalized three-parameter dark energy equation-of-state parametrization, compares it to observational cosmological data using statistical model selection (e.g., likelihood or information criteria), and analyzes its dynamical behavior relative to ΛCDM and the original Barboza-Alcaniz model.
AI.result: The new parametrization is statistically preferred by current cosmological data over both the Barboza-Alcaniz model and ΛCDM; it yields qualitatively similar cosmological evolution but with a slightly reduced cosmic acceleration rate.
AI.conclusion: The proposed generalization provides a more robust and empirically supported description of dark energy dynamics, particularly at future times, without sacrificing simplicity or physical interpretability.

title: Carroll fermions of arbitrary spin
summary: Electric and magnetic Carrollian actions for fermions of arbitrary spin in any spacetime dimension are defined as inequivalent $c \to 0$ limits of the relativistic Fang-Fronsdal actions.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs electric and magnetic Carrollian actions for fermions of arbitrary spin in any spacetime dimension by taking distinct c → 0 limits of the relativistic Fang–Fronsdal actions.
AI.motivation: To systematically define consistent Carrollian (ultra-relativistic, c → 0) fermionic field theories for arbitrary spin in general dimensions, addressing the lack of well-defined Carrollian limits for higher-spin fermions.
AI.method: Systematic c → 0 limiting procedure applied to the relativistic Fang–Fronsdal action for fermionic higher-spin fields, yielding two physically inequivalent Carrollian limits—electric and magnetic—distinguished by their scaling behavior and gauge structure.
AI.result: Explicit electric and magnetic Carrollian Lagrangians for fermions of arbitrary spin in D-dimensional spacetime; identification of their respective gauge symmetries, constraint structures, and physical degrees of freedom.
AI.conclusion: Carrollian fermionic higher-spin theories admit two distinct consistent formulations, enriching the landscape of non-Lorentzian field theories and enabling future studies of flat-space holography and ultra-relativistic symmetry breaking.

title: The leading-soft cubic graviton self-interaction on the black-hole horizon
summary: We expand the Einstein-Hilbert action to cubic order about the Schwarzschild horizon, in the even Regge-Wheeler gauge of the Gaddam-Groenenboom-'t~Hooft (GGV) near-horizon framework, and derive the cubic graviton self-interaction. Our central result is a `vanishing theorem': at leading soft order the self-coupling of the purely traceless longitudinal polarizations is identically zero, because with the trace/transverse-scalar sector switched off the fluctuation reduces to a two-dimensional block whose $\sqrt{-g}\,R$ is a total (Euler) derivative at every order in $κ$. We prove this by an explicit closed-form reduction and exhibit the cancellation term by term. It is a `framework-specific' statement, even RW gauge, GGV sector, leading soft order, not a gauge-invariant theorem of general relativity. The theorem is exact, but the quantized vertex inherits a $\sim\!20\%$ soft/scheme systematic at the only simulable multiplet ($\ell=2$), which we state explicitly. We then simulate the real-time dynamics of the resulting Hamiltonian on IBM Qiskit/Aer with exact cross-checks. Two structural facts, a conserved charge that only the cubic vertex violates, opening $φφ\to hh\to4φ$, and a provably resonance-free boost spectrum (gap $\to1/2$), already predict that the longitudinal channel is perturbatively rigid; the simulation confirms this quantitatively and measures the residual dressing ($d_{\rm eff}=1.06$; multiplicity far from thermal, Poisson, and Haar references) rather than discovering it. A symmetry-exact total-occupation truncation yields the first sector-resolved level statistics, indicative of intermediate behaviour on Hilbert spaces too small to be decisive. All circuit results agree with exact diagonalization, every headline number carries a stated systematic, and hardware execution is deferred behind a quantified noise budget.

AI.tldr: The paper derives the cubic graviton self-interaction near the Schwarzschild horizon in the GGV framework and even Regge-Wheeler gauge, proving a 'vanishing theorem' for traceless longitudinal polarizations at leading soft order—due to topological (Euler-derivative) cancellation in √−g R. The result is framework-specific, exact classically, but incurs ~20% soft/scheme systematic in quantized ℓ=2 vertex simulations on IBM Qiskit/Aer. Real-time dynamics confirm perturbative rigidity of the longitudinal channel, evidenced by conserved-charge violation, resonance-free boost spectrum, and measured residual dressing (d_eff = 1.06); level statistics suggest intermediate quantum chaos.
AI.motivation: To understand graviton self-interactions near black hole horizons within a controlled near-horizon effective framework (GGV), specifically probing whether longitudinal modes couple at leading soft order—a question tied to consistency, unitarity, and quantum gravity phenomenology in extreme curvature regimes.
AI.method: Expansion of the Einstein-Hilbert action to cubic order in metric fluctuations about Schwarzschild in even Regge-Wheeler gauge within the GGV near-horizon coordinates; explicit closed-form reduction showing √−g R becomes a total Euler derivative when trace/transverse-scalar sector is decoupled; Hamiltonian derivation and real-time quantum simulation on IBM Qiskit/Aer with exact diagonalization cross-checks; symmetry-exact truncation for level statistics; systematic error quantification including soft/scheme and noise budgets.
AI.result: Proof of a framework-specific vanishing theorem: cubic self-coupling of purely traceless longitudinal polarizations identically vanishes at leading soft order; numerical simulation confirms longitudinal channel rigidity, yielding d_eff = 1.06, non-thermal/non-Poisson/non-Haar occupation multiplicity, and resonance-free boost spectrum with gap → 1/2; first sector-resolved level statistics from symmetry-exact truncation; all circuit outputs validated against exact diagonalization; every quantitative claim carries stated systematics.
AI.conclusion: The longitudinal graviton sector exhibits perturbative rigidity near the Schwarzschild horizon in the GGV/RW framework—not due to generic GR symmetries, but due to a topological cancellation mechanism operative at leading soft order. This rigidity is numerically robust (despite ~20% scheme dependence at ℓ=2), and the observed residual dressing and spectral statistics suggest emergent integrability or constrained dynamics rather than chaotic thermalization.

title: Energy-Energy Correlators at Strong Coupling
summary: We study energy-energy correlators (EEC) in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory at strong 't Hooft coupling $λ$. We consider the EEC in states created by half-BPS operators of arbitrary dimension $p$, and determine the corresponding event-shape function up to order $λ^{-3/2}$ from the worldsheet representation of the AdS Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude with Kaluza-Klein external states. For $p=2$ we compute the second curvature correction, which completes the EEC through order $λ^{-2}$; the new contribution improves the agreement with recently derived non-perturbative bounds at intermediate coupling. We further develop a complementary method in which the strong-coupling expansion coefficients of the EEC are extracted directly from the Wilson coefficients of low-energy expansion of the AdS Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude, and find the two approaches in perfect agreement.

AI.tldr: This paper computes energy-energy correlators (EEC) in planar N=4 SYM at strong coupling using worldsheet and Wilson coefficient methods, achieving precision up to λ^{-2} for p=2 and λ^{-3/2} for general p, and validating results against non-perturbative bounds.
AI.motivation: To extend the understanding of event-shape observables like EEC beyond leading order in the strong-coupling expansion, test consistency between different AdS/CFT computational frameworks, and confront predictions with rigorous non-perturbative bounds.
AI.method: Two complementary approaches: (1) worldsheet representation of the AdS Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude with Kaluza-Klein external states to compute EEC for half-BPS states of dimension p; (2) extraction of EEC coefficients from low-energy Wilson coefficients of the same amplitude.
AI.result: EEC determined up to O(λ^{-3/2}) for arbitrary p; for p=2, second curvature correction computed, completing full O(λ^{-2}) result; both methods yield identical coefficients; improved agreement with non-perturbative bounds at intermediate coupling.
AI.conclusion: The two independent AdS/CFT methods for computing EEC agree precisely, confirming robustness of the holographic dictionary for event shapes; higher-order corrections are essential for quantitative comparison with bounds, highlighting the role of curvature corrections in precision holography.

title: Spin-mediated modulation of chaos bound violation in Lorentz-violating black hole spacetimes
summary: We investigate how the particle spin modulates chaos bound violations in Lorentz-violating black hole spacetimes within the framework of Bumblebee gravity. By analyzing spinning charged particles in static spherically symmetric (A)dS black holes, we reveal the roles of spin--curvature coupling, Lorentz symmetry breaking, and the cosmological constant in shaping chaotic dynamics. The results show that the spin provides a fine-tuning mechanism for the chaos bound violation by modifying the critical angular momentum threshold, allowing particles with larger spin to access the violation regime at lower angular momenta. The Lorentz-violating parameter suppresses the violations by narrowing the allowed parameter region and reducing the critical charge. Meanwhile, the cosmological constant exhibits a dual influence: a more negative cosmological constant decreases the parameter region of violation while enhancing the violation magnitude for configurations that remain beyond the bound. These findings demonstrate that the spin and Lorentz symmetry breaking effects jointly modify the relationship between orbital instability and horizon properties.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how particle spin affects chaos bound violations in Lorentz-violating black hole spacetimes within Bumblebee gravity, revealing spin–curvature coupling, Lorentz breaking, and cosmological constant jointly tune chaotic dynamics.
AI.motivation: To understand how intrinsic particle spin, Lorentz symmetry violation, and cosmological constant influence chaos bound violations in black hole spacetimes described by Bumblebee gravity.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical investigation of chaotic dynamics of spinning charged particles in static, spherically symmetric (A)dS black hole backgrounds with Lorentz violation induced by the Bumblebee field.
AI.result: Spin lowers the critical angular momentum threshold for chaos bound violation; Lorentz-violating parameter suppresses violations by shrinking the allowed parameter space and reducing critical charge; negative cosmological constant shrinks violation region but amplifies violation magnitude for surviving configurations.
AI.conclusion: Particle spin and Lorentz symmetry breaking co-modulate the link between orbital instability and black hole horizon structure, enabling fine-tuned control over chaos bound violations.

title: Defect entanglement entropy for superconformal RG Interfaces
summary: We study the defect contribution to the entanglement entropy of a spherical region centred on four-dimensional superconformal RG interfaces. These interfaces are supersymmetric codimension one defects separating the Leigh--Strassler SCFT vacuum and the $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM theory deformed by spatially varying mass terms. Exploiting the holographic dual to these interfaces, we extract a cutoff-independent interface contribution to the entanglement entropy, $\mathcal{C}^I$. We quantify the non-trivial dependence of $\mathcal{C}^I$ on the supersymmetric mass deformation, and observe a scaling regime for large deformations. We further relate $\mathcal{C}^I$ to the renormalized on-shell action and the stress-tensor one-point function of the interface theory. Our results provide the first fully backreacted holographic computation of this entanglement quantity for superconformal RG interfaces in more than two dimensions.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the cutoff-independent entanglement entropy contribution (C^I) from supersymmetric RG interfaces in 4D via holography, links it to on-shell action and stress-tensor one-point function, and reveals scaling behavior under large mass deformations.
AI.motivation: To compute the defect contribution to entanglement entropy for superconformal RG interfaces in more than two dimensions — a previously unaddressed problem — using fully backreacted holography.
AI.method: Holographic computation using the dual gravitational background of four-dimensional superconformal RG interfaces separating Leigh–Strassler SCFT and spatially deformed N=4 SYM; extraction of cutoff-independent interface entropy C^I; analysis of its dependence on supersymmetric mass deformation and relation to renormalized on-shell action and stress-tensor one-point function.
AI.result: A well-defined, cutoff-independent interface entanglement entropy C^I is obtained; its non-trivial dependence on the supersymmetric mass deformation is quantified; a large-deformation scaling regime is identified; C^I is shown to be related to both the renormalized on-shell action and the interface stress-tensor one-point function.
AI.conclusion: This work provides the first fully backreacted holographic calculation of defect entanglement entropy for superconformal RG interfaces in D > 2, establishing concrete connections between interface entropy, bulk on-shell action, and boundary stress-tensor expectation values.

title: Zipoy--Voorhees spacetime with Maxwell and dilaton fields: exact solution and equatorial geodesics
summary: We derive a new exact solution of four-dimensional Kaluza-Klein theory by applying the uplift-boost-reduction procedure to the Zipoy-Voorhees vacuum seed. The resulting Zipoy-Voorhees-dilaton spacetime is a static, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat configuration parametrised by a seed length scale $M$, the Zipoy-Voorhees deformation parameter $k$, and a boost parameter $α$ that controls the electric charge. For $k=1$ it admits a regular black-hole interpretation; for $k \neq 1$ it inherits the naked curvature singularity of the seed at $r=2M$. We extract the ADM mass, electric charge, and dilaton charge, finding that the dilaton charge obeys an algebraic constraint independent of the quadrupole deformation. The equatorial geodesics of neutral test particles and photons are studied in detail. A compact algebraic identity locates the exterior-photon-ring threshold at $k=1/2$ for all $α$, generalising the known threshold of the vacuum Zipoy-Voorhees case. The innermost stable circular orbit is mapped over the $(k,α)$ plane, and the comparison with Schwarzschild is shown to depend qualitatively on whether seed-mass or ADM-mass units are used. We further compute the gravitational redshift, which diverges on the $r=2M$ surface and renders the near-singularity orbits effectively invisible, and the critical impact parameter setting the characteristic shadow size, which in ADM-mass units shrinks below the Schwarzschild value as the charge grows.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a new exact solution in 4D Kaluza-Klein theory—the Zipoy-Voorhees-dilaton spacetime—via uplift-boost-reduction of the Zipoy-Voorhees vacuum seed; it analyzes its geometric and physical properties including mass, charge, geodesics, photon rings, ISCO, redshift, and shadow size.
AI.motivation: To generate a physically rich, exact charged, deformed black-hole-like solution in Kaluza-Klein gravity that generalizes the vacuum Zipoy-Voorhees metric and enables systematic study of deformation–charge interplay in strong-field relativistic phenomena.
AI.method: Uplift-boost-reduction procedure applied to the Zipoy-Voorhees vacuum seed in 5D Kaluza-Klein theory, followed by dimensional reduction to 4D; analytical computation of conserved charges (ADM mass, electric and dilaton charges), geodesic analysis (equatorial timelike and null), photon-ring threshold derivation, ISCO mapping, redshift evaluation, and shadow-size (critical impact parameter) calculation.
AI.result: A three-parameter static, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat Zipoy-Voorhees-dilaton solution; identification of k=1 as regular black hole case and r=2M singularity for k≠1; algebraic dilaton-charge constraint; photon-ring threshold at k=1/2 independent of α; ISCO behavior qualitatively dependent on mass normalization; divergent redshift at r=2M; shadow size (in ADM-mass units) decreasing with increasing charge α.
AI.conclusion: The solution provides a versatile testbed for probing strong-gravity effects of simultaneous quadrupole deformation and dilatonic charge in Kaluza-Klein gravity; key observables (photon ring, ISCO, shadow) exhibit nontrivial dependence on k and α, revealing qualitative shifts relative to Schwarzschild and highlighting the role of mass definition in physical interpretation.

title: Diagonally gauged anomaly-free 6D supergravities and their vacua
summary: We describe a bounded search for local and global anomaly-free six-dimensional $(1,0)$ models with tensor number $T=1$ and gauge group containing a diagonal abelian factor $U(1)_{R+}$. The abelian factor is the diagonal combination of the usual gauged $U(1)_R$ and a $U(1)\subset Sp(n_H)$ acting on hypermultiplets. We have searched for locally and globally anomaly-free $G_1\times U(1)_{R+}$ and $G_1\times G_2\times U(1)_{R+}$ models, subject to restrictions on the ranks of the simple factors and on the maximal charges carried by matter. We find that, unlike the case of $U(1)_R$ gauged models which are relatively rare, the diagonally gauged ones offer a rich landscape. We also study the 6D vacua of these models and find that they admit supersymmetric 6D Minkowski vacua, for which the diagonal nature of the R-symmetry gauging is necessary.

AI.tldr: This paper explores anomaly-free 6D (1,0) supergravity models with T=1 tensor multiplet and a diagonally gauged U(1)_{R+} symmetry—combining the R-symmetry U(1)_R and a flavor U(1)⊂Sp(n_H)—and identifies a rich landscape of such models, unlike the sparse U(1)_R-only cases; it further shows that supersymmetric 6D Minkowski vacua require this diagonal gauging.
AI.motivation: To systematically construct and classify locally and globally anomaly-free six-dimensional (1,0) supergravity theories with T=1 and a diagonal abelian gauging U(1)_{R+}, motivated by the scarcity of standard U(1)_R-gauged models and the need to understand viable supersymmetric vacua and matter charge constraints.
AI.method: Bounded search over gauge groups G₁×U(1)_{R+} and G₁×G₂×U(1)_{R+}, imposing consistency conditions: six-dimensional gravitational, gauge, and mixed anomaly cancellation (local and global), rank bounds on simple factors, and upper limits on hypermultiplet U(1)_{R+} charges; supplemented by analysis of scalar potentials and vacuum solutions.
AI.result: A rich set of anomaly-free models with diagonal U(1)_{R+} gauging is found—contrasting sharply with the rarity of pure U(1)_R models; all supersymmetric 6D Minkowski vacua identified require the diagonal structure of the R-symmetry gauging.
AI.conclusion: Diagonal gauging of R-symmetry significantly expands the space of consistent 6D (1,0) supergravity models and is essential for realizing supersymmetric Minkowski vacua, suggesting its fundamental role in model building and UV completions (e.g., F-theory).

title: Cosmological initial data without periodic boundary conditions
summary: We apply the parabolic-hyperbolic formulation of the Einstein constraint equations to generate cosmological initial data. The freely specifiable geometric data correspond to flat Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker background, while the matter sector contains localized anisotropic perturbations of a perfect fluid. Unlike the standard approach, our method evolves the constraints outward from regular data at the origin and therefore requires no boundary conditions. This makes our method well suited as a starting point in investigating systematic biases introduced by commonly adopted boundary conditions, such as periodic boundaries. A second advantage concerns uniqueness: standard elliptic solvers may fail when multiple solutions exist, whereas solving the constraints as a well-posed evolutionary system always yields a unique solution. To demonstrate our method, we implement it numerically and generate cosmological initial data with localized anisotropic perfect fluid perturbations.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a parabolic-hyperbolic formulation of the Einstein constraint equations to construct cosmological initial data without boundary conditions, enabling unique solutions and facilitating study of boundary-induced biases.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of standard elliptic solvers—namely dependence on artificial boundary conditions (e.g., periodic) and non-uniqueness when multiple solutions exist—in generating physically realistic cosmological initial data.
AI.method: Uses a parabolic-hyperbolic reformulation of the Einstein constraints, evolving outward from regular initial data at the origin; avoids boundary conditions entirely; implemented numerically for localized anisotropic perfect fluid perturbations on a flat FLRW background.
AI.result: Successful numerical generation of cosmological initial data with localized anisotropic perfect fluid perturbations; demonstrates uniqueness and boundary-condition independence.
AI.conclusion: The parabolic-hyperbolic approach provides a robust, unique, and boundary-free alternative to elliptic methods for solving the Einstein constraints, particularly valuable for assessing systematic biases from conventional boundary treatments in cosmological simulations.

title: High-Order Pole-Skipping in Near-Extremal Holography
comment: 17 pages, many figures,2 tables, Phys. Rev.D in press
summary: We develop a systematic analytic method for studying high-order pole-skipping in near-extremal holographic black holes. In the near-extremal regime, approaching the limit $T\to0$, the near-horizon geometry develops an approximately $\mathrm{AdS}_2 \times \mathbb{R}^{d-1}$ structure; we show that the mode index $q$ labeling pole-skipping points is identified with the IR conformal dimension $Δ_{\mathrm{IR}} = q$ in the emergent $\mathrm{AdS}_2/\mathrm{CFT}_1$ correspondence, providing a concrete physical interpretation of the subleading pole-skipping tower. The method reorganizes the near-horizon Frobenius expansion according to powers of temperature. This reveals a temperature-graded hierarchical structure that reduces the $n$-th-order pole-skipping condition to a factorized algebraic equation:each pole-skipping momentum depends only on the mode index $q$, not on the order $n$. This $n$-independence produces a high degeneracy as $T\to 0$, where pole-skipping momenta at all orders collapse onto a discrete set of values determined by near-horizon geometry and the scalar field mass; these values can be expressed in terms of thermodynamic quantities such as entropy density and specific heat. In the limit $n \gg 1$ (with $nT$ remaining small), the leading pole-skipping momenta grow asymptotically as $k_{n,n} \propto n$. We compute leading temperature corrections and verify our predictions through numerical analysis of the Dyonic Gubser--Rocha model. The results confirm that high-order pole-skipping at low temperature is governed by near-horizon physics. This provides analytic access to pole-skipping points well beyond those accessible by standard determinant methods and clarifies the structure of holographic Green's functions in the low-temperature regime.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an analytic method to study high-order pole-skipping in near-extremal holographic black holes, linking pole-skipping momenta to IR conformal dimensions in emergent AdS₂/CFT₁, revealing a temperature-graded hierarchy where pole-skipping momenta become order-independent and degenerate at low T, governed solely by near-horizon geometry and thermodynamics.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand high-order pole-skipping — a hallmark of quantum chaos and non-analyticity in holographic Green's functions — in the physically relevant near-extremal (low-temperature) regime, where standard determinant-based numerical methods fail.
AI.method: A temperature-graded Frobenius expansion near the horizon of near-extremal black holes; reorganization of perturbative equations by powers of T; identification of pole-skipping conditions with eigenvalue problems tied to AdS₂ isometries; analytical factorization of n-th-order conditions; validation via numerical solution of the Dyonic Gubser–Rocha model.
AI.result: Pole-skipping momenta k_{n,q} at order n depend only on mode index q (i.e., IR conformal dimension Δ_IR = q), not on n — leading to T→0 degeneracy onto discrete values expressible via entropy density and specific heat; asymptotically, k_{n,n} ∝ n for large n; leading T-corrections computed and numerically verified.
AI.conclusion: High-order pole-skipping in near-extremal holography is governed entirely by near-horizon AdS₂ physics and thermodynamics; the temperature-graded analytic framework provides exact control over pole-skipping structure beyond reach of conventional methods, clarifying the low-T behavior of holographic correlators.

title: Octupole moments and the non-universality of free-fall in general relativity
summary: Extended bodies in general relativity do not necessarily fall along geodesics, but can be accelerated. These accelerations depend on an object's angular momentum, as well as on its quadrupole, octupole, and higher-order moments. However, these multipole moments can evolve differently from one body to another. Different bodies can thus fall differently, even with identical initial data. This paper examines how octupole moments contribute to the non-universality of free-fall in general relativity. We begin by showing that in arbitrary vacuum spacetimes, only the trace-free component of an octupole moment can affect an object's motion. It follows that at least 16 out of 40 octupole components decouple from the laws of motion. Then, we obtain two decompositions for trace-free octupole moments, one in terms of a timelike frame vector and the other in terms of a null tetrad. These decompositions are applied to motion both in generic Newtonian spacetimes and in fully-relativistic vacuum spacetimes that are of Petrov type D. In Newtonian spacetimes, the mass moments are shown to have their ordinary Newtonian effects, while the momentum moments determine a body's hidden momentum---the misalignment between its momentum and its velocity. In Petrov type D spacetimes (such as Kerr), we show that some torques that are impossible with quadrupole moments are possible with octupole moments. Octupole moments can thus have qualitatively-different effects from quadrupole moments.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how octupole moments—beyond mass and quadrupole—break the universality of free-fall in general relativity; it proves only the trace-free part influences motion (decoupling 16 of 40 components), provides frame- and tetrad-based decompositions, and shows octupole-induced torques absent at quadrupole order, especially in Petrov type D (e.g., Kerr) spacetimes.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher multipole moments—specifically octupole—contribute to non-geodesic motion and break the universality of free-fall, beyond known quadrupole effects.
AI.method: Analytical derivation using multipole expansions in general relativity; identification of trace-free octupole constraints in arbitrary vacuum spacetimes; decomposition into timelike-frame and null-tetrad bases; application to Newtonian limits and Petrov type D vacuum solutions (e.g., Kerr).
AI.result: Only the trace-free octupole (24 components) couples to motion—16 components decouple; two physically distinct decompositions are constructed; in Newtonian limits, momentum octupoles generate hidden momentum; in Petrov type D spacetimes, octupole moments enable new torque configurations forbidden for quadrupoles.
AI.conclusion: Octupole moments introduce qualitatively new gravitational self-interaction effects not reducible to lower multipoles, fundamentally enriching the dynamics of extended bodies and violating universality of free-fall in ways inaccessible to quadrupole-only models.

title: Wilson Towers as Local Bulk Fields
summary: Multi-winding Wilson loops (``Wilson spools'') in 2+1-dimensional gravity can reproduce one-loop partition functions of local free fields in the bulk. Bulk free fields have a second-quantized Fock space, and the AdS/CFT correspondence suggests that the associated multi-particle sectors are dual to multi-trace primaries in the CFT. In this note, we use standard symmetric-function methods to show that the Wilson spool in thermal AdS$_3$ can be recast as a sum over $single$-winding Wilson loops --- one for each multi-trace primary. In a companion paper to appear, we will view Wilson networks and TQFTs as the natural language of non-perturbative bulk quantum gravity. The present note illustrates how this can apply to $local$ bulk fields, and not just defects: a bulk (generalized free) field is to be viewed as a full tower of multi-trace Wilson lines. We further show that the $SL(2)$ descendants of each multi-trace primary, together with the boundary gravitons of the AdS$_3$ background, correctly reproduce the full Virasoro character of each module. In this language, the role of a light insertion on a heavy primary is played by a topological Verlinde line. This allows us to obtain a ``microscopic" description of one-loop determinants on the smooth BTZ handlebody. A spatially wound probe Wilson line on a torus with a contractible $thermal$ cycle can be traded for a Verlinde line inserted on a dense family of heavy Polyakov loops --- with the roles of the two cycles exchanged, so that the $spatial$ cycle is now contractible. The vacuum row of the modular $S$-kernel acts as the (approximate) density of the heavy primaries. This reinforces the case made in arXiv:2601.18775 that a smooth horizon is a stand-in for an ensemble of quantum states, each produced by a heavy Wilson line that appears as a singular horizon in the semi-classical limit.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that multi-winding Wilson loops ('Wilson spools') in 2+1D gravity encode one-loop partition functions of bulk local free fields; using symmetric-function techniques, it recasts the thermal AdS₃ Wilson spool as a sum over single-winding Wilson loops—each associated with a multi-trace primary—and demonstrates how SL(2) descendants and boundary gravitons reconstruct full Virasoro characters; it interprets bulk generalized free fields as towers of multi-trace Wilson lines, identifies topological Verlinde lines as duals to light insertions on heavy primaries, and uses this framework to microscopically derive one-loop determinants on the BTZ handlebody, linking smooth horizons to ensembles of heavy Wilson-line states.
AI.motivation: To reconcile local bulk quantum field theory with non-perturbative holography by interpreting multi-winding Wilson loops (Wilson spools) as encoding Fock-space structure of bulk free fields and connecting them to multi-trace CFT primaries—thereby bridging perturbative bulk physics with topological, non-perturbative gravitational degrees of freedom.
AI.method: Applies symmetric-function theory to decompose multi-winding Wilson loops in thermal AdS₃ into sums over single-winding loops labeled by integer partitions; constructs Virasoro characters from SL(2) descendants and boundary gravitons; identifies topological Verlinde lines as duals to light operator insertions; uses modular S-kernel vacuum row to approximate heavy primary density; leverages duality between spatially wound Wilson lines and Verlinde lines on dense Polyakov loops with exchanged thermal/spatial cycle roles.
AI.result: Wilson spools are exactly equivalent to sums over single-winding Wilson loops indexed by multi-trace primaries; Virasoro characters emerge from SL(2) descendants + boundary gravitons; Verlinde lines provide microscopic description of one-loop determinants on BTZ; smooth horizons correspond to statistical ensembles of heavy Wilson-line states, not single geometries.
AI.conclusion: Local bulk fields in AdS₃ gravity are holographically encoded not as individual Wilson lines but as infinite towers of multi-trace Wilson lines—i.e., Wilson spools—whose decomposition reveals deep connections between symmetric function combinatorics, Virasoro representation theory, topological line operators, and the statistical nature of black hole horizons.

title: A story about a tipsy kangaroo: Reversible jump MCMC for model selection in the analysis of gravitational-wave signals from the coalescence of compact objects
summary: Bayesian inference is commonly employed in the analysis of gravitational-wave signals not only to estimate the source parameters, but also for model selection. The latter provides insight into the physics of the source and has the potential to inform the direction for future model development. Although model comparison is usually performed by analyzing the data separately with different models and comparing the obtained Bayesian evidences, an alternative approach consists in sampling directly over the model itself. Here, we present t-roo, a reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler capable of performing transdimensional inference on gravitational-wave signals from compact binary coalescences. Employing t-roo, a single analysis provides simultaneously the model odds ratio and the parameter posteriors for the favored models, hence yielding a potentially substantial computational advantage, particularly when comparing many models or analyzing highly informative data. t-roo is built on the sampler eryn and is specifically designed to compare models describing different kinds of sources, i.e., binary black hole, binary neutron star, or neutron star-black hole systems, as well as multiple models for the same source class. We validate the sampler on a set of injections, finding agreement with the results obtained with the nested sampler dynesty. We then use t-roo to analyze the real events GW190425 and GW230529, for which the system's parameters alone do not provide conclusive evidence of the presence of a neutron star component. t-roo can be adapted to any model-comparison scenario, thus providing a valuable tool in particular for next-generation detectors, where analyzing data separately with competing models becomes computationally even more demanding.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces t-roo, a reversible jump MCMC sampler for transdimensional Bayesian inference in gravitational-wave astronomy, enabling simultaneous model comparison and parameter estimation—particularly for distinguishing compact binary types (BBH, BNS, NSBH)—with computational advantages over traditional nested sampling.
AI.motivation: To overcome the computational inefficiency of performing separate Bayesian analyses for each model when comparing multiple gravitational-wave source models, especially as data volume and model complexity increase with next-generation detectors.
AI.method: Develops t-roo, a reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo (rjMCMC) sampler built on eryn, designed for transdimensional inference over discrete model spaces (e.g., BBH vs. BNS vs. NSBH) and continuous parameter spaces; validated against dynesty on simulated injections and applied to real events GW190425 and GW230529.
AI.result: t-roo correctly recovers model odds ratios and parameter posteriors, agreeing with dynesty on injections; analysis of GW190425 and GW230529 yields quantitative model probabilities for neutron-star-containing systems where standard parameter estimation is inconclusive.
AI.conclusion: t-roo provides an efficient, unified framework for Bayesian model selection and parameter inference in gravitational-wave astrophysics, scalable to multi-model comparisons and suitable for future high-SNR, high-throughput detector data.

title: Relational path integral, effective actions and quantum frame covariance
summary: We propose a relational bundle-geometric formulation of the gravitational path integral by invoking the new tool of quantum reference frames (QRFs), which in gravity are gauge-covariant coordinate systems constructed from the available field content. Formulated in terms of relational (frame-dressed) observables, this yields a manifestly gauge-invariant path integral without ghosts and anomalies, and in which observables and their correlators are local to a frame. While eliminating the need for gauge fixing, it is equivalent to Faddeev-Popov versions in which the QRF is gauge-fixed, recovering certain previous proposals. A key feature is its covariance under QRF changes: it is a perspective-neutral path integral which encodes all internal QRF perspectives and the transformations between them. This leads to several qualitative predictions: local correlators and time evolution of relational observables in one QRF perspective become fuzzy in another, and a new spectrum of relational vacua arises. Comprised of frame-dependent no-boundary and asymptotic ground states, a vacuum from one perspective appears generally excited in another. Finally, we construct gauge-invariant, yet frame-dependent effective actions by coupling sources exclusively to relational observables, setting the stage for a relational definition of renormalization.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a relational, bundle-geometric formulation of the gravitational path integral using quantum reference frames (QRFs), yielding a manifestly gauge-invariant, ghost- and anomaly-free framework where observables are local to a QRF; it is perspective-neutral—encoding all QRF perspectives and transformations—and predicts frame-dependent locality, time evolution fuzziness, relational vacua, and enables relational renormalization via frame-dressed effective actions.
AI.motivation: To resolve conceptual and technical issues in quantum gravity—specifically, the reliance on gauge fixing, presence of ghosts/anomalies, and lack of physical interpretability of observables—by formulating the gravitational path integral in terms of relational, gauge-covariant quantum reference frames constructed from dynamical fields.
AI.method: Develops a bundle-geometric reformulation of the gravitational path integral using quantum reference frames (QRFs) as gauge-covariant, field-based coordinate systems; defines relational (frame-dressed) observables; constructs a perspective-neutral path integral that encodes all internal QRF perspectives and their interconversion; derives frame-dependent effective actions by coupling sources only to relational observables.
AI.result: A manifestly gauge-invariant gravitational path integral without ghosts or anomalies; equivalence to Faddeev-Popov approaches upon QRF gauge-fixing; covariance under QRF changes; prediction of frame-dependent locality and fuzziness of correlators/time evolution; emergence of a spectrum of relational vacua (e.g., no-boundary/asymptotic ground states) that are frame-dependent and generally excited across perspectives; construction of gauge-invariant yet frame-dependent effective actions.
AI.conclusion: Relational QRFs provide a physically transparent, mathematically rigorous foundation for quantum gravity's path integral, replacing arbitrary gauge choices with dynamical, observable-based frames—enabling a consistent, perspective-neutral formalism with testable qualitative consequences for locality, vacuum structure, and renormalization.

title: A universal scaling function for giant graviton OPE coefficients
summary: We consider the large spin limit $S\to\infty$ of the OPE coefficient for two maximal giant gravitons and a spinning operator with finite twist in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory. Up to an overall normalization factor, this OPE coefficient exhibits a power-law scaling of the form $S^{d(g)}$. We provide strong evidence that the exponent $d(g)$ is free from finite size corrections. Consequently, the all-loop asymptotic expression for the OPE coefficient can be used to determine $d(g)$ exactly. We develop a systematic method to compute the scaling function $d(g)$ for arbitrary values of the 't Hooft coupling $g$. At weak coupling, our result agrees perfectly with the available field-theoretic results up to three-loop order. At strong coupling, we present the first three orders as concrete predictions. We further provide the finite-coupling result and show that it interpolates smoothly between the weak- and strong-coupling regimes.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the large-spin asymptotics of OPE coefficients involving two maximal giant gravitons and a finite-twist spinning operator in planar N=4 SYM, showing the exponent d(g) of the power-law scaling S^{d(g)} is free from finite-size corrections and computing it exactly across all 't Hooft coupling g.
AI.motivation: To determine the exact large-spin scaling behavior of OPE coefficients in planar N=4 SYM, bridging weak- and strong-coupling regimes and testing integrability-based predictions beyond finite-size effects.
AI.method: Uses integrability-based all-loop asymptotic OPE formalism; develops a systematic method to compute the scaling exponent d(g) as a function of 't Hooft coupling g, leveraging freedom from finite-size corrections.
AI.result: Demonstrates d(g) is finite-size correction-free; computes d(g) exactly at weak coupling (matching field-theory up to three loops), predicts first three orders at strong coupling, and provides smooth finite-coupling interpolation.
AI.conclusion: The exponent d(g) governing the S^{d(g)} scaling of the OPE coefficient is universal and exactly computable via integrability; its smooth interpolation confirms consistency of the asymptotic OPE framework across the full coupling range.

title: Aspects of Closed Matricial Worlds
summary: We investigate the Hilbert space structure for simple theories of gravity with $Λ>0$ on closed spatial sections. Our motivation ties to the presence of gravitational saddles in four-dimensional $Λ>0$ Einstein-Maxwell theory with $S^2\times Σ_h$ topology, where $Σ_h$ is a genus-$h$ Riemann surface. Here, as a concrete starting point, the problem is explored for two-dimensional $Λ>0$ quantum gravity. We revisit and elaborate on exact results in the matrix model literature. We study gravitational wavefunctions from both the perspective of the Wheeler-DeWitt equation and the gravitational path integral. Though simple, the setting displays many features of general interest such as large volume effects that disrupt the perturbative expansion, topological corrections to the path-integral wavefunction that offend the exact Wheeler-DeWitt equation, and a sphere path integral ${Z}^{(0)}_{\text{grav}}$ with non-trivial structure in $Λ$. We discuss candidate inner products for the infinite-dimensional canonical gravitational Hilbert space uncovered by Lian and Zuckerman. By establishing explicit results up to genus-six, we argue that the dominant contribution to the genus-$h$ gravitational disk path integral at large spatial size mimics the behavior of two-dimensional topological gravity. In passing, we show that for ${Z}^{(0)}_{\text{grav}}$ to give rise to a positive counting problem for discretised Riemann surfaces, it must have a negative pre-factor. We contrast our analysis to the more realistic case of timelike Liouville theory.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the Hilbert space structure of simple Λ > 0 gravity theories on closed spatial sections, using 2D quantum gravity as a tractable model; it reconciles Wheeler–DeWitt wavefunctions with path-integral results, identifies non-perturbative and topological effects, and proposes inner products for the canonical gravitational Hilbert space.
AI.motivation: To understand the Hilbert space structure of de Sitter-like gravity (Λ > 0) on closed spatial sections, motivated by gravitational saddles in 4D Einstein-Maxwell theory with S² × Σₕ topology.
AI.method: Analyzes 2D Λ > 0 quantum gravity via exact matrix model results, Wheeler–DeWitt equation solutions, and gravitational path integrals; computes genus-expansion up to h = 6; compares with topological gravity and timelike Liouville theory.
AI.result: Identifies large-volume breakdown of perturbation theory, topological corrections violating exact Wheeler–DeWitt consistency, nontrivial Λ-dependence of the sphere partition function Z⁽⁰⁾_grav, and asymptotic genus-h disk amplitudes mimicking 2D topological gravity; shows Z⁽⁰⁾_grav requires negative prefactor for positive discretized surface counting.
AI.conclusion: The canonical gravitational Hilbert space—previously uncovered by Lian–Zuckerman—is physically realized only with careful choice of inner product; non-perturbative and topological features are essential even in 2D, informing broader quantum gravity in de Sitter settings.

title: Revealing the conformal symmetry of the discrete series scalars in dS${}_2$
summary: On two-dimensional manifolds with nonzero constant Ricci curvature, there exists an infinite sequence of scalar fields with nonzero mass parameter that admit a pair of (anti)-holomorphic currents. After suitably defining the theory in de Sitter space ($\mathrm{dS}_2$), correlation functions of these currents obey global conformal Ward identities. We address the question of how this global conformal symmetry manifests as an action on the scalar field. An essential step is in leveraging an equivalent description of the scalar field in terms of a conformal Killing tensor. Through this, we find a conformal symmetry transformation that acts locally on the conformal Killing tensor, but non-locally on the scalar field. We show that the equation of motion transforms covariantly with respect to these conformal transformations, and further find a traceless stress tensor in both $\mathrm{dS}_2$ and $\mathrm{AdS}_2$, locally defined in terms of the conformal Killing tensor, which generates the global conformal isometry transformations.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies an infinite family of massive scalar fields on 2D manifolds with constant Ricci curvature that support (anti)-holomorphic currents; it constructs a local conformal symmetry action via conformal Killing tensors, establishes covariance of the equations of motion, and defines a local, traceless stress tensor generating global conformal isometries in both dS₂ and AdS₂.
AI.motivation: To understand how global conformal symmetry manifests as a local symmetry transformation on massive scalar fields admitting (anti)-holomorphic currents in two-dimensional de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spaces.
AI.method: Leverages an equivalent formulation of the scalar field in terms of a conformal Killing tensor; constructs conformal transformations acting locally on the tensor but non-locally on the scalar field; verifies covariance of the equation of motion; constructs a locally defined, traceless stress tensor generating global conformal isometries.
AI.result: A conformal symmetry transformation acting non-locally on the scalar field but locally on its associated conformal Killing tensor; covariance of the scalar field’s equation of motion under these transformations; existence of a local, traceless stress tensor in both dS₂ and AdS₂ that generates global conformal isometries.
AI.conclusion: Global conformal symmetry in dS₂ and AdS₂ for massive scalar fields with (anti)-holomorphic currents is realized through a non-local action on the scalar field, yet admits a local geometric description via conformal Killing tensors and a corresponding local stress tensor.

title: On the strong coupling limit of Yang-Mills matrix models
summary: We study the strong coupling limit of mass deformed Yang--Mills matrix models, with the aim of understanding when the matrices become effectively commuting. The Yang--Mills interaction classically drives the matrices toward mutually commuting valleys, where the matrices can potentially be interpreted as coordinates of an emergent space. However, taking into consideration the integration measure, commutativity is not automatic since the commuting locus is entropically suppressed, and in the bosonic models with $D\geq3$ the strong coupling limit remains non-commuting. We find that fermions change this competition in a sharp way. As the number of fermionic degrees of freedom is increased, there is a critical value $\mathcal N_c=2(D-2)$, realized by the supersymmetric Yang--Mills matrix models, at which the matrices commute at strong coupling. The same critical models also exhibit universality under deformations by $O(N^2)$, or huge, operators: the normalized eigenvalue densities are insensitive to the microscopic details of the huge operators. Increasing the number of fermions beyond the critical point still gives commuting matrices, but the huge-operator universality is lost. Thus commutativity and universality are related but distinct: the matrix models with supersymmetric field content sit at the critical boundary where we have both.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the strong-coupling behavior of mass-deformed Yang--Mills matrix models, showing that fermions induce a critical transition to commuting matrices at N_c = 2(D−2), coinciding with supersymmetric models; at this critical point, eigenvalue statistics also exhibit universality under large deformations.
AI.motivation: To determine when matrices in Yang--Mills matrix models become effectively commuting—enabling interpretation as emergent spacetime coordinates—and to understand the role of fermions versus bosonic entropy in driving or suppressing commutativity.
AI.method: Analytical study of the strong coupling limit of mass-deformed Yang--Mills matrix models, comparing bosonic and fermionic contributions to the path integral measure; identification of critical fermion count via competition between Yang--Mills potential (favoring commutativity) and measure-induced entropy (disfavoring it); analysis of eigenvalue density response to O(N²) 'huge' operators.
AI.result: A sharp critical fermion count N_c = 2(D−2) is found: below it, matrices remain non-commuting; at it (realized by SYM models), matrices commute and eigenvalue densities exhibit universality under huge operator deformations; above it, commutativity persists but universality is lost.
AI.conclusion: Commutativity and huge-operator universality are distinct but co-occur precisely at the supersymmetric critical point; supersymmetry thus marks a special boundary in the space of matrix models where emergent geometry and robust spectral statistics coincide.
